question: What kinds of drugs can impair your driving ability?
options: a:Only illegal drugs.,b:No drugs affect driving if taken as directed.,c:Only prescription medicines.,d:Illegal, prescription, and over-the-counter drugs can all impair driving.
note: Many types of drugs can impair driving, including illegal drugs, prescription medications, and over‑the‑counter medicines. Even when taken as directed, some drugs can cause drowsiness, slow reaction time, or affect judgment. Always read labels and talk to your doctor or pharmacist about how a medicine may affect your ability to drive safely.

question: If your vehicle's accelerator sticks open, what is the correct response?
options: a:Shift to neutral, turn on hazard lights, apply brakes gradually, and safely pull off the road, then turn off the ignition.,b:Slam the brakes and hold them down hard.,c:Keep accelerating to reach a safe area quickly.,d:Turn the steering wheel sharply to stall the engine.
note: If your accelerator sticks, keep calm and quickly shift to neutral so the engine is no longer driving the wheels. Turn on your hazard lights, steer smoothly, and apply the brakes gradually to slow down and move to the side of the road. Once you are safely off the roadway and stopped, then turn off the ignition. Do not turn the key to lock while moving, because that can lock the steering.

question: On a two-lane road without bicycle lanes, the safest way to pass a bicyclist is to:
options: a:Honk and expect the bicyclist to move over.,b:Force them off the road by driving quickly past.,c:Pass as close as possible to minimize time near them.,d:Slow down, wait until it is safe, and pass with at least 3 feet of clearance (more at higher speeds).
note: When passing a bicyclist on a two‑lane road without a bike lane, slow down and wait until it is safe to move over and give them plenty of space—at least 3 feet, and more at higher speeds. Only pass when you can do so without crowding the bicyclist or oncoming traffic. Never honk aggressively, crowd, or try to force a bicyclist off the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do speed limit signs legally indicate?
options: a:Potential driving speeds for the area.,b:The maximum or minimum speed that is legally allowed under ideal conditions.,c:The speed drivers should drive in heavy traffic.,d:A recommended speed for inexperienced drivers.
note: Speed limit signs show the maximum (and sometimes minimum) speed allowed under ideal conditions. You must slow down below the posted limit when conditions such as rain, fog, traffic, or road work make it unsafe to travel at the maximum speed. The posted limit is never a guarantee that it is safe to drive that fast in all situations.

question: Why is a leaking exhaust system hazardous?
options: a:Carbon monoxide poisoning.,b:A loss of hearing.,c:Pollution.
note: A leaking exhaust system is dangerous because it can let carbon monoxide and other exhaust gases enter the passenger compartment. Carbon monoxide is colorless and odorless and can cause headache, dizziness, unconsciousness, and death. Any suspected exhaust leak should be checked and repaired immediately.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging from an entrance ramp onto a crowded freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a gap.,b:Use mirrors and blind-spot checks and use the acceleration lane to match freeway speed.,c:Enter immediately without checking.,d:Yield only to vehicles on your left.
note: When entering a freeway, use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to reach the speed of traffic on the freeway, then merge when there is a safe gap. Check your mirrors and blind spots, signal, and always yield to vehicles already on the freeway. Stopping at the end of the ramp is unsafe because other drivers do not expect a stopped vehicle there.

question: You hear a siren behind you while driving. What should you do?
options: a:Speed up to get out of the way.,b:Safely pull over to the right and stop to allow the emergency vehicle to pass.,c:Ignore it if you do not see lights.,d:Stop immediately where you are and remain.
note: When an emergency vehicle using sirens and/or flashing lights approaches, you must yield the right-of-way. Safely pull over to the right side of the road and stop until the vehicle has passed, unless directed otherwise by law enforcement. Do not speed up or stop suddenly in the lane, as that can create additional hazards.

question: Which factor greatly increases stopping distance and the seriousness of a crash?
options: a:Night driving.,b:Slow speeds.,c:High speeds.
note: As speed increases, your stopping distance grows rapidly because both your reaction distance and braking distance get longer. In a crash, higher speed also means much greater impact force, which increases the likelihood of serious injury or death. Driving at safe, legal speeds gives you more time and space to react and stop.

question: What does a single broken yellow line down the center of a two-lane road mean?
options: a:Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is prohibited.,b:You must not cross for any reason.,c:Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed when it is safe.,d:It marks a bicycle lane.
note: A single broken yellow line in the center of a two-lane road means traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed from either direction when it is safe and legal. Before passing, you must ensure there is enough clear distance ahead, no oncoming traffic close by, and no signs or markings prohibiting passing.

question: At a railroad crossing without flashing warnings or gates, how should you proceed?
options: a:Approach with caution and be prepared to yield to any train, ensuring room to clear the tracks.,b:Cross immediately to save time.,c:Always stop no matter what.,d:Shift gears while crossing to avoid stalling.
note: At a railroad crossing without lights or gates, slow down, look and listen carefully in both directions, and be prepared to stop. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming and there is enough space on the far side of the tracks for your vehicle to clear completely. Never stop on the tracks or shift gears while crossing.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and keep moving in your lane.,b:Pull to the right curb and stop.,c:Keep driving in your lane and ignore it.,d:Speed up to clear the way.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights and/or siren, you must safely pull over to the right side of the road and stop, remaining stopped until it has passed. This creates a clear path so the emergency vehicle can move quickly and safely.

question: If you are in the left lane and want to move to the right lane, what is the correct procedure?
options: a:Check mirrors only and change lanes.,b:Check mirrors and look over your shoulder in the direction you are moving before changing.,c:Check mirrors only.,d:Signal and immediately swing into the right lane.
note: Before changing lanes, always check your mirrors, signal, and then look over your shoulder in the direction you are moving to check your blind spot. If you are moving to the right lane, you look over your right shoulder; if moving to the left lane, you look over your left shoulder. Only move when the lane is clear and it is safe.

question: Where should you try to maintain a space cushion when driving?
options: a:Only on the left and right sides of your vehicle.,b:On all sides of your vehicle.,c:Only in front of your vehicle.
note: A space cushion is the open space around your vehicle that gives you time to react. You should maintain space in front, behind, and on both sides whenever possible so you can brake, change lanes, or steer away from hazards safely.

question: What does a double solid yellow line down the center of a two-lane road indicate?
options: a:Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is prohibited in both directions.,b:Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is prohibited.,c:You may pass if no oncoming traffic appears.,d:You may use the shoulder to pass.
note: A double solid yellow line separates traffic moving in opposite directions and means passing is not allowed from either direction. You must stay in your lane and may only cross these lines when making a permitted left turn or when directed by traffic control or emergency personnel.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn on a solid red light (where allowed), you must:
options: a:Only signal after you begin turning.,b:Come to a complete stop, then yield to pedestrians and other traffic before turning if not prohibited by signs.,c:Turn immediately without stopping.,d:Wait for the light to turn green no matter what.
note: Where right turns on red are allowed, you must first come to a complete stop at the limit line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection. After stopping, yield to pedestrians and all other traffic with the right-of-way. Only turn when the way is clear and no signs prohibit a right turn on red.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a highway from a driveway or private road, you should:
options: a:Yield to vehicles on your left only.,b:Drive quickly onto the road to merge.,c:Yield to traffic on the highway.,d:Assume you have the right-of-way.
note: When entering a highway from a driveway or private road, you must yield to all traffic already on the highway. Vehicles on the main road have the right-of-way, and you may enter only when there is a safe gap. Never assume others will slow down or move for you.

question: When may you cross a dashed white line?
options: a:Only if there are no other vehicles on the road.,b:When it is safe to change lanes.,c:Only during daylight.,d:Never.
note: A dashed (broken) white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross it when it is safe to change lanes or pass, after checking mirrors, blind spots, and signaling. You must not change lanes if it would interfere with another vehicle.

question: When driving in fog you should use:
options: a:High beam headlights to see further.,b:Parking lights only.,c:Hazard lights while moving.,d:Low beam headlights (and fog lights if equipped).
note: In fog, use low beam headlights because high beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and can make it harder to see. If your vehicle has fog lights, use them with low beams. Drive at a speed that allows you to stop within the distance you can see.

question: If an approaching driver fails to dim high beams, where should you look?
options: a:Toward the left side of the road.,b:At the approaching vehicle's wheels.,c:Toward the right side of the road to avoid glare.,d:Directly into the headlights to show them you're blinded.
note: If an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, avoid looking directly into the glare. Instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane or the right side of the road, using it as a guide, while still checking the road ahead periodically. This helps protect your night vision and keeps you in your lane.

question: When changing lanes on most roads, you should:
options: a:Make a lane change without checking blind spots to be quick.,b:Begin signaling well before the lane change and check mirrors and blind spots.,c:Signal as you start the lane change and then check your mirrors.,d:Only check mirrors and then change lanes without signaling.
note: When changing lanes, signal well in advance, then check your mirrors and your blind spots by quickly turning your head to look over your shoulder. Change lanes only when it is safe and smooth to do so. Signaling early (about 100 feet in lower-speed areas or several seconds on freeways) lets other drivers anticipate your move.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you approach an intersection with a flashing yellow light?
options: a:Stop and wait for the light to change.,b:Turn around because the intersection is closed.,c:Proceed through the intersection with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light means you do not need to stop, but you must slow down, look carefully in all directions, and proceed through the intersection with caution. Be prepared to yield to pedestrians and other vehicles that have the right‑of‑way.

question: When are roads most dangerous in terms of traction relative to rain?
options: a:After it has been raining for several hours.,b:Just as it begins to rain,c:When it stops raining completely.,d:Only during heavy thunderstorms.
note: Roads are most slippery just as it begins to rain, especially after a dry spell. The first rainwater mixes with oil and dirt on the road surface, creating a slick film that greatly reduces traction until it is washed away.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it acceptable to go through an intersection with a stop sign but no stop line or crosswalk?
options: a:After slowing to verify no cross traffic.,b:After stopping at least 20 feet from the intersection.,c:After coming to a complete stop and confirming it's safe.,d:After yielding to pedestrians only.
note: At a stop sign with no stop line or crosswalk, you must come to a complete stop before entering the intersection, usually at the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you have a clear view of traffic. After stopping fully and checking for vehicles and pedestrians, proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you on a two-lane road, what should you do?
options: a:Decrease your speed further.,b:Not allow other cars to pass your vehicle.,c:Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.,d:Turn on your hazard lights and continue slowly.
note: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you on a two‑lane road, you should safely pull off to the right side of the road or into a turnout area and let the vehicles behind you pass. This helps prevent driver frustration and reduces the risk of unsafe passing maneuvers.

question: If you suffer a tire blowout while driving, you should:
options: a:Take your foot off the accelerator, do not immediately brake hard, gradually slow, and pull off the road.,b:Slam on the brakes immediately to stop quickly.,c:Turn the steering wheel sharply to the right and stop in the travel lane.,d:Speed up to reduce wobble.
note: During a tire blowout, hold the steering wheel firmly, take your foot off the accelerator, and avoid hard or sudden braking. Let the vehicle slow down gradually while you keep it going straight, then carefully steer to the side of the road and stop in a safe place.

question: When it starts to sleet or snow while you are driving, you should:
options: a:Maintain normal following distance but increase speed to get home faster.,b:Keep windshield and mirrors clear and increase your following distance.,c:Turn on your high beams to better see the road ahead.,d:Ignore other vehicles and drive normally.
note: In sleet or snow, traction is reduced and stopping distances increase. You should keep your windshield and mirrors clear for maximum visibility and increase your following distance so you have more time and space to stop smoothly on slippery roads.

question: If stopped by a police officer, how should you behave?
options: a:Get out immediately and approach the officer.,b:Stay in your vehicle with hands visible on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach.,c:Open your door and shout your license number.,d:Unbuckle your seat belt and exit the vehicle.
note: When stopped by police, staying in your vehicle with your hands visible on the steering wheel helps the officer see that you are not a threat. Wait for instructions before reaching for documents or exiting the vehicle, and follow the officer’s directions calmly and respectfully.

question: Which of these can impair driving ability?
options: a:Alcohol.,b:Any medication.,c:A lack of sleep.,d:All of the above.
note: Driving can be impaired by alcohol, many legal and illegal drugs (including some medications), and by drowsiness or lack of sleep. Any of these can slow your reaction time, affect judgment, and reduce awareness, making driving unsafe.

question: If you hit an unattended parked vehicle and can't find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Stay until police arrive, even if you have already left your information.,b:Leave without taking any action.,c:Drive to the nearest service station and report it there.,d:Leave a written notice with your name, address, and an explanation of the accident in a secure, visible place on the vehicle.
note: If you hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, you must stop and leave a written notice in a secure, visible place on the vehicle. The note should include your name, address, and an explanation of the accident, and you must report the collision as required by state law.

question: How should you safely pass a bicyclist?
options: a:Drive in the bicycle lane to pass.,b:Honk to alert them before passing.,c:Slow down and give as much space as possible.,d:Pass quickly without changing lane position.
note: When passing a bicyclist, slow down and give them as much space as possible, following your state’s minimum passing distance (often at least 3 feet, and more at higher speeds). Do not crowd the bicyclist or drive in the bike lane; change lane position or lanes if needed to pass safely.

question: Does drinking coffee after alcohol reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Yes — it cancels the alcohol's effect.,b:No — it does not affect BAC.,c:It instantly sober you up.,d:It increases BAC.
note: Caffeine or coffee does not lower BAC; it may make you more alert but does not reduce alcohol levels in your system.

question: Where are stop lines painted and what do they indicate?
options: a:In curves and on hills.,b:Next to churches and schools.,c:At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
note: Stop lines are solid white lines painted across the approach lanes at intersections and before pedestrian crosswalks. They show drivers exactly where they must stop at a red light, stop sign, or when required for pedestrians, so the vehicle stays out of the crosswalk and intersection.

question: What is the recommended response when another driver behaves aggressively?
options: a:Retaliate by tailgating.,b:Cut them off to slow them down.,c:Avoid eye contact.
note: When another driver is aggressive, your goal is to avoid escalating the situation. Stay calm, avoid eye contact, do not make gestures, and do not retaliate. If possible, create space by slowing slightly and letting them go ahead. This reduces the chance of a confrontation or crash.

question: When approaching an accident scene, what should you do if you are not involved?
options: a:Keep your attention on your driving and pass without stopping unless emergency help hasn't arrived and you can safely assist.,b:Stop and get out to watch the scene.,c:Pile into the area to take photographs.,d:Slow down to look and impede traffic.
note: If you are not involved in a crash, keep your attention on driving and pass carefully without stopping. Only stop if emergency help has not arrived and you can safely assist without creating more danger. Unnecessary stopping or slowing to look can cause additional crashes and traffic delays.

question: How can you best avoid alcohol-related crashes?
options: a:Decide before you start drinking that you will not drive.,b:Say no when someone offers you a drink if you're already drinking.,c:Drink water between alcoholic drinks so you can drive later.
note: The safest way to avoid alcohol‑related crashes is to decide in advance that you will not drive after drinking and to arrange a sober ride, such as a designated driver, taxi, or rideshare. Once you start drinking, your judgment is impaired, making it harder to make safe decisions about driving.

question: How should you approach a railroad crossing that has no signals?
options: a:Speed through to minimize time on the tracks.,b:Slow down,c:Always stop regardless of visibility.,d:Assume crossings without signals are always safe.
note: At a railroad crossing without signals, you must slow down, look, and listen carefully for trains. Be prepared to stop if a train is approaching, and only proceed when you are sure the tracks are clear and it is safe to cross.

question: What can happen if you drink alcohol while using prescription or over-the-counter medicine?
options: a:Nothing significant will occur.,b:The combination could multiply the effects of the alcohol or medicine.,c:The alcohol will make the medicine more effective.,d:The medicine will cancel the alcohol's effects.
note: Alcohol can interact with prescription and over‑the‑counter medicines and greatly increase drowsiness, dizziness, and slowed reaction time. The combination can impair your driving much more than either substance alone, even if you feel only mildly affected.

question: When is it appropriate to sound your horn?
options: a:To signal impatience in traffic.,b:When passing another car.,c:If you've lost control of your vehicle to warn others.,d:To greet friends driving nearby.
note: Use your horn only to warn others of a safety problem, such as when you lose control or when another driver or pedestrian may not see you. Do not use the horn to show anger, impatience, or to greet people.

question: What does a crossbuck sign identify?
options: a:School zones.,b:Railroad crossings.,c:No passing zones.,d:Pedestrian crosswalks.
note: A crossbuck sign marks a railroad crossing. It means you must yield to trains, slow down, look and listen for approaching trains, and be prepared to stop. Never try to beat a train through the crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it allowed to cross double solid yellow lines?
options: a:To pass a slow-moving passenger car when safe.,b:To pass another car going the same direction.,c:To make a left turn into or from a driveway,d:To overtake bicyclists at any time.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and mean no passing. You may not cross them to pass, but you may carefully cross to make a left turn into or out of a driveway, private road, or alley when it is safe and legal.

question: Which of these is a common cause of traffic collisions?
options: a:Excessive speed for conditions,b:Following other vehicles too closely.,c:Inattentive driving
note: Crashes often have multiple contributing factors, but driving at a speed that is too fast for road, traffic, or weather conditions is one of the leading causes of serious collisions. Excessive speed reduces your time to react and increases stopping distance and crash severity, which is why it is emphasized as a major cause.

question: Does the type of alcoholic beverage (beer vs. wine) change how alcohol affects your reflexes and judgment?
options: a:No — impairment depends on amount consumed,b:Only hard liquor impairs driving.,c:Yes — mixed drinks are more impairing.,d:Yes — beer affects you less than wine.
note: Alcohol affects your brain and body based on how much pure alcohol you consume, your body size, and how quickly you drink it—not whether it comes from beer, wine, or liquor. A standard drink of beer, wine, or spirits contains about the same amount of alcohol and can impair judgment, coordination, and reaction time equally.

question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, how should you react?
options: a:Call the police immediately while driving erratically.,b:Try to block them from passing.,c:Flash your lights to reprimand them.,d:Stay calm and move out of their way.
note: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, the safest response is to stay calm, avoid eye contact or gestures, and create space by slowing down or changing lanes when safe. Do not try to retaliate or engage with the driver, as this can quickly escalate into road rage or cause a collision.

question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
options: a:Bad weather.,b:Poor road design.,c:Human error.,d:Mechanical failure.
note: The vast majority of crashes are caused by human error, such as inattention, distraction, following too closely, speeding, or misjudging gaps and speeds. While weather, road design, and mechanical problems can contribute, driver behavior is the primary factor in most collisions.

question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching with siren or lights, what should you do?
options: a:Drive as far right as possible and stop, taking care not to stop in an intersection.,b:Continue at the same speed if you are not in the emergency vehicle's path.,c:Speed up and pull away from the emergency vehicle.,d:Stop immediately in your lane wherever you are.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights or siren, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling as far to the right side of the road as is safe and stopping, being careful not to stop in an intersection. Remain stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed, unless directed otherwise by officials.

question: Which statement about winter driving is NOT true?
options: a:Checking antifreeze and washer fluid is important.,b:Snow tires can improve traction.,c:Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.,d:Winter is the most difficult driving season.
note: Using cruise control on snow, ice, or in other slippery winter conditions is unsafe because it can cause your wheels to spin or lose traction before you can react. In winter you should check antifreeze and washer fluid, consider snow tires for better traction, and recognize that winter is generally the most difficult driving season due to reduced visibility and slippery roads.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Traffic signals sometimes display arrows to control turns from specific lanes. What does a solid yellow arrow mean?
options: a:It indicates a pedestrian-only phase is starting.,b:It is never used in traffic signals.,c:It has the same meaning as a circular yellow light and you should prepare to stop.,d:It means you may immediately turn in the arrow's direction without yielding.
note: A solid yellow arrow means the protected turning movement is ending and a red arrow is about to appear. It has the same meaning as a circular yellow light for that lane: slow down and prepare to stop if you can do so safely, and do not enter the intersection to start the turn once the yellow arrow appears.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of these statements about passing is true?
options: a:You should return to your lane before seeing the passed vehicle's headlights in your mirror.,b:Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes,c:Do not signal when passing to avoid confusion.,d:Only use your mirrors
note: When passing, you must signal before changing lanes—typically at least 100 feet before on most roads—so other drivers know your intentions. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to clear your blind spot. After passing, return to your lane only when you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady yellow traffic light at an intersection mean?
options: a:Go through the intersection quickly.,b:The signal is malfunctioning.,c:Slow down and prepare to stop,d:Yield to other cars and continue at the same speed.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You should slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop safely when it turns yellow, you may proceed with caution, but you should not speed up to beat the red light.

question: What type of signs warn drivers about hazardous conditions ahead?
options: a:Guide signs.,b:Information signs.,c:Warning signs.,d:Regulatory signs.
note: Warning signs are typically yellow and black and alert drivers to hazards or changes in road conditions ahead, such as curves, intersections, pedestrian crossings, or animal crossings. Regulatory signs, usually white with black or red lettering, tell you about laws and regulations you must obey, such as speed limits or no‑parking zones.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection with a yield sign, you should:
options: a:Only yield to traffic on your left.,b:Always come to a complete stop,c:Ignore it if no traffic is present.,d:Slow and yield the right-of-way to traffic in the roadway you are entering.
note: At a yield sign, you must slow down and be prepared to stop. You must let any traffic, bicyclists, or pedestrians already in or close to the intersection go first. If the way is clear, you do not have to stop, but you must still approach at a safe, reduced speed and be ready to yield the right-of-way.

question: Why must drivers be extra alert to motorcycles, bicyclists, and pedestrians?
options: a:They always travel at the same speed as cars.,b:They are smaller and harder to see,c:They obey completely different laws.,d:They always have the right-of-way.
note: Motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians are smaller and can be hidden in blind spots or blend into the background, making them harder to see. Because they are more vulnerable in a crash, drivers must scan carefully, check mirrors and blind spots, and anticipate their movements to avoid collisions.

question: When parallel parking between two cars, your first step should be to:
options: a:Reverse quickly into the space.,b:Pull up even with the car in front of the space before beginning to back in.,c:Turn your wheels immediately toward the curb.,d:Angle into the space without aligning with neighboring cars.
note: For standard parallel parking, you first pull up parallel and even with the vehicle in front of the space, leaving a safe gap. From this position you then back slowly while turning the wheel as needed. Lining up with the front vehicle gives you the correct angle and space to enter the spot safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are you required to stop your vehicle?
options: a:At an intersection with a stop sign.,b:When a traffic officer orders you to stop.,c:At a red traffic light.,d:All of the above.
note: You must come to a complete stop at stop signs, at red traffic lights (unless a specific sign or signal allows movement), and any time a traffic officer directs you to stop. Obeying these controls is essential for right-of-way, safety, and legal compliance at intersections and on the roadway.

question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line indicates:
options: a:Vehicles next to the broken line may pass when safe, while those next to the solid line may not.,b:Passing is prohibited from both directions.,c:Both lanes may pass at any time.,d:The road is one-way.
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is allowed only for traffic on the side with the broken line, and prohibited for traffic on the side with the solid line. This marking is used where passing is safe in one direction but too risky in the other due to limited visibility or other hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is it unsafe and illegal to pass another vehicle?
options: a:On the shoulder of the road.,b:When the passing lane is clear and marked with a broken yellow line.,c:On a hill or in a curve where you cannot see oncoming traffic.,d:On a multilane expressway with three lanes.
note: You must never pass where you cannot see far enough ahead to be sure the way is clear, such as on hills or curves. Passing on the shoulder is also illegal because the shoulder is not a travel lane and may contain stopped vehicles, pedestrians, or debris. Only pass in clearly marked passing zones when you have a safe, clear view and enough space to complete the maneuver without speeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the usual speed limit on open county highways in West Virginia?
options: a:65 mph.,b:55 mph.,c:70 mph.,d:60 mph.
note: In West Virginia, the general speed limit on open county highways is 55 mph unless signs show a different limit. Always obey posted signs, as local conditions may require lower or higher speeds than the general rule.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:
options: a:Signal only when other vehicles are present.,b:Signal briefly as you begin the turn only.,c:Always signal your intentions in advance,d:Signal only at night.
note: You must always signal before turning or changing lanes so other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians know what you plan to do. Turn on your signal well in advance—typically at least 100 feet before turning in town and farther at higher speeds—and keep it on until the maneuver is completed.

question: Compared to daytime driving, driving at night is:
options: a:The same if headlights are used.,b:No more or less dangerous.,c:More dangerous.,d:Less dangerous.
note: Driving at night is more dangerous than daytime driving because you can see less of the road ahead, it is harder to judge distances and speeds, and glare from headlights can reduce visibility. There is also a higher chance of encountering fatigued or impaired drivers. Use extra caution, reduce speed as needed, and keep your headlights and windshield clean.

question: If an approaching vehicle fails to dim its high beams, where should you look to avoid glare?
options: a:The right side of the road.,b:The center of the road.,c:Either side at random.,d:Directly into the headlights.
note: If an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, avoid looking directly at the bright lights. Instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane or the right side of the road. This reduces glare while helping you stay correctly positioned in your lane until the vehicle passes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering an interstate from an entrance ramp, you should:
options: a:Stop on the ramp and wait for an opening in traffic.,b:Enter at any speed,c:Adjust your speed to match traffic and merge safely after locating a gap.,d:Drive on the shoulder briefly and merge when safe.
note: Use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to reach the speed of traffic on the interstate, check mirrors and blind spots, find a safe gap, and then merge smoothly without stopping on the ramp.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:When you need to warn another road user of immediate danger, such as a child stepping into the street.,b:When traveling through an intersection.,c:To greet acquaintances on the sidewalk.,d:When passing a bicyclist on a quiet road.
note: Use your horn only to warn others of immediate danger, such as when someone is about to step or move into your path and may not see you. Avoid using the horn to express anger, greet people, or for unnecessary noise.

question: What must a driver do when an emergency vehicle using lights or siren approaches?
options: a:Pull to the right and stop immediately.,b:Slow down and continue driving to the right.,c:Turn on four-way flashers and continue moving.,d:Speed up to clear the lane.
note: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or siren approaches from any direction, safely move to the right side of the road and stop until it has passed, unless directed otherwise by a police officer.

question: When may you not cross a single broken white or yellow line?
options: a:When crossing would interfere with traffic or be unsafe.,b:When turning left into a driveway.,c:When the vehicle in front is disabled.,d:When passing is allowed.
note: A single broken line means you may cross it to pass or change lanes only when it is safe and will not interfere with other traffic. If crossing would force others to slow or swerve, or visibility is poor, you must not cross.

question: A pedestrian begins crossing in front of your vehicle. What should you do?
options: a:Sound your horn continuously.,b:Speed up and pass in front of them.,c:Flash your lights to warn them.,d:Slow down and be prepared to stop.
note: Always yield to pedestrians crossing the roadway and be prepared to stop, especially in crosswalks and near children.

question: What must you do when you see a steady green arrow at a traffic signal?
options: a:Always stop and wait for a green circular light.,b:Merge immediately without yielding.,c:Turn only if there is no oncoming traffic at any speed.,d:You may turn in the arrow's direction after yielding to vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection.
note: A green arrow permits the indicated turn, but you must still yield to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a steady yellow traffic light, drivers should:
options: a:Turn on hazards.,b:Slow and stop if safe unless already in the intersection.,c:Ignore it because green still has priority.,d:Speed up to beat the red.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You should slow down and stop if you can do so safely. If you are too close to the intersection to stop safely when the light turns yellow, continue through with caution rather than braking abruptly.

question: Before starting the vehicle, what safety step should you do?
options: a:Buckle your seat belt and ensure passengers are buckled.,b:Be sure only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.,c:Make sure only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.,d:Start the car and then buckle.
note: Develop a routine of buckling your seat belt and ensuring all passengers are restrained before switching on the ignition.

question: What best describes defensive driving?
options: a:Racing to get ahead of poor drivers.,b:Following the vehicle ahead closely to control traffic.,c:Identifying hazardous driving situations and acting to avoid crashes.,d:Adjusting your driving to prevent collisions by anticipating and responding to potential hazards.
note: Defensive driving means staying aware of your surroundings, spotting potential hazards early, and adjusting your speed, position, and actions to avoid collisions. You leave yourself a safety margin, anticipate mistakes by other drivers, and respond calmly and safely rather than aggressively.

question: How should a seat belt be properly worn?
options: a:Is loose.,b:Is buckled snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.,c:Is hidden beneath the seat.,d:Is worn with the lap belt low on the hips and the shoulder belt across the chest and shoulder.
note: A seat belt should fit snugly, not loosely. The lap belt must rest low across your hip bones and lower abdomen, never across the stomach alone, and the shoulder belt should cross the middle of your chest and shoulder, away from your neck and face. Proper fit helps the belt hold your body securely in a crash and reduces the risk of serious injury.

question: Which of the following does NOT occur after drinking alcohol?
options: a:You are less alert.,b:You become more alert.,c:Your judgment of speed and distance is distorted.,d:Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.
note: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows your brain and body, making you less alert, slowing your reflexes, and distorting your judgment of speed and distance. Becoming more alert is not an effect of drinking alcohol.

question: What color pavement markings separate traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:Red.,b:White.,c:Blue.,d:Yellow.
note: Yellow pavement markings are used to separate traffic moving in opposite directions. White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction, and other colors are used for special purposes such as parking or restrictions, not for separating opposing traffic.

question: When driving in poor weather, drivers should:
options: a:Decrease their following distance.,b:Increase their following distance.,c:Maintain the same following distance as in good weather.,d:Increase their speed to clear hazardous areas quicker.
note: In poor weather, roads are more slippery and visibility is reduced, so it takes longer to see hazards and to stop. You should increase your following distance to give yourself more time and space to react safely.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, you should:
options: a:Steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go (generally in the same direction as the skid) and avoid overcorrecting.,b:Turn the steering wheel into oncoming traffic always.,c:Brake hard and hold the wheel firmly straight.,d:Turn away from the skid and slam the brakes.
note: If your vehicle begins to skid, stay calm, ease off the accelerator, and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go, which is generally the same direction the rear of the vehicle is skidding. This helps you regain traction and control. Avoid slamming on the brakes or jerking the wheel, as overcorrecting can cause a spin.

question: How must a driver behave toward pedestrians in or near the roadway?
options: a:Yield only when the pedestrian is legally entitled to it.,b:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.,c:Make sure the pedestrian is aware of your vehicle before proceeding.
note: Drivers must exercise great care around pedestrians and do everything reasonably possible to avoid hitting them. You should be prepared to yield to pedestrians in or near the roadway, even if they are crossing improperly, because they are more vulnerable and you are responsible for operating your vehicle safely.

question: When driving through an area where children are playing, what should you expect?
options: a:That children will always wait for traffic to clear.,b:That a child may suddenly run into the street without looking.,c:That children will remain on the sidewalk.,d:That children will obey crossing guards at all times.
note: Children playing near the road are unpredictable and may suddenly run into the street without looking. When you see children, slow down, cover the brake, and be prepared to stop at any moment, even if they appear to be on the sidewalk or near a crossing guard.

question: When driving on highways, how should you maintain alertness?
options: a:Stare straight ahead to avoid distractions.,b:Rely on cruise control exclusively.,c:Keep your eyes moving and be ready to react to hazards.,d:Look at one thing for a long time to focus.
note: On highways, you prevent drowsiness and highway hypnosis by constantly scanning: look far ahead, check mirrors frequently, and watch to the sides for potential hazards. Keeping your eyes moving helps you notice changing traffic and gives you more time to react safely.

question: Which traffic control device requires you to come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go when safe?
options: a:A solid red light.,b:A solid green light.,c:A flashing yellow light.,d:A flashing red light.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just like at a stop sign. After stopping, yield to any traffic or pedestrians with the right-of-way, and proceed only when the road is clear and it is safe to go.

question: Before backing out of a driveway with children nearby, you should:
options: a:Sound your horn loudly to warn children.,b:Exit the vehicle and walk to the rear to ensure the way is clear.,c:Rev the engine so they notice you are moving.,d:Back up slowly while watching through mirrors only.
note: Before backing out where children may be present, walk behind your vehicle to check for children, toys, or other obstacles in your blind zone. Children are small and can be hidden from mirrors and cameras, so physically checking behind the vehicle is the safest practice.

question: If a transit (bus) is signaling to re-enter traffic after stopping, you must:
options: a:Remain in your lane and ignore the signal.,b:Speed past before they merge.,c:Yield and allow them to safely re-enter.,d:Sound your horn to warn them.
note: When a bus signals that it is pulling away from a stop, you should be prepared to yield so it can re-enter traffic safely. Slow down, change lanes if possible, or stop if needed to avoid cutting off the bus. This reduces conflicts and helps large vehicles merge smoothly.

question: When must drivers yield to pedestrians?
options: a:Even if the pedestrian crosses the street carelessly.,b:Only when the pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk.,c:Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as the driver.
note: Drivers must always be prepared to yield to pedestrians who are in the roadway, even if the pedestrian is crossing carelessly or outside a crosswalk. The law and basic safety principles require drivers to do whatever is necessary to avoid hitting a person, because pedestrians are much more vulnerable in a collision.

question: When you approach a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:
options: a:Maintain your speed and stay in your lane.,b:Speed up to clear the area quickly.,c:If possible, move over a lane or, if you cannot safely change lanes, slow down and pass with caution.,d:Stop immediately in your lane.
note: Give stopped emergency or roadside vehicles as much space as possible by changing lanes or slowing down safely if a lane change is unsafe.

question: What colors are used on highway signs that tell you distances or destinations (such as the next exit)?
options: a:Red background with white letters.,b:Black background with white letters.,c:Yellow background with black letters.,d:Green background with white letters.
note: Guide signs that show directions, destinations, and distances on highways are green with white letters or symbols. These signs help you find exits, cities, and routes while traveling.

question: Your blind spot refers to the area:
options: a:Directly behind your vehicle as seen in the rearview mirror.,b:You cannot see without moving your head (not visible in mirrors).,c:Inside the vehicle cabin near the driver.,d:Covered by your side mirrors.
note: A blind spot is any area around your vehicle that you cannot see by using your mirrors alone. To check your blind spots, you must briefly turn your head and look over your shoulder before changing lanes or merging. Relying only on mirrors can cause you to miss vehicles, bicycles, or motorcycles traveling alongside you.

question: When must you stop for a school bus that is loading or unloading children?
options: a:If it is parked on the shoulder with no one in it.,b:When it approaches you even if its lights are not flashing.,c:If you are driving on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.
note: On a two-lane road, traffic in both directions must stop when a school bus is stopped with its red lights flashing and/or its stop arm extended. You must remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn, because children may be crossing the road from either side.

question: On which signal do you have the right-of-way to turn left?
options: a:A solid green circular light.,b:A flashing yellow light.,c:A green arrow pointing left.,d:A steady red arrow to the left.
note: A green left arrow is a protected turn signal. When it is lit, oncoming traffic and pedestrians facing you have a red light, so you have the right‑of‑way to turn left. A solid green circle or flashing yellow means you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians; a red arrow means no turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a heavy truck from behind on an uphill, what should you expect?
options: a:It is always legal to pass on a hill if you have room.,b:The truck may be traveling slower than the posted limit and you may not be able to safely pass on a hill.,c:The truck will always keep up with posted speeds.,d:The truck will automatically pull over to let you pass.
note: Heavy trucks often slow down on upgrades because of their weight. On hills, your view of oncoming traffic is limited, so passing may be unsafe or illegal even if the truck is below the speed limit. You must only pass when you have clear sight distance and it is legally permitted.

question: Which statement is correct about alcohol's effect on driving?
options: a:Alcohol does not affect driving when consumed with food.,b:Even small amounts of alcohol can impair concentration,c:Only a BAC above the legal limit impairs driving.,d:Alcohol improves calmness and reaction time.
note: Even a small amount of alcohol can slow reaction time, reduce judgment, and affect concentration. Food does not prevent impairment, and driving can be unsafe well before you reach the legal BAC limit. Alcohol never improves driving performance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a fire engine is following you on a two-lane street but is not using emergency signals, you should:
options: a:Continue driving in a normal manner, you are not required to yield unless it is using sirens or lights.,b:Pull over and stop immediately.,c:Speed up to get out of its way.,d:Stop in the middle of the street to allow it by.
note: You are required to yield the right‑of‑way to emergency vehicles only when they are using their lights and/or siren. If a fire engine is behind you without emergency signals, drive normally, obeying speed limits and lane rules. Do not stop in the lane or speed up unnecessarily.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, you should turn the steering wheel:
options: a:To keep the front wheels straight and locked.,b:In the opposite direction of the skid immediately.,c:In the direction you want the vehicle to go (into the skid).,d:Sharp and fast away from the skid.
note: In a skid, look and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go. This is often described as steering "into the skid." As the vehicle begins to straighten, gently adjust the steering to avoid overcorrecting and losing control again.

question: How can you help prevent hydroplaning?
options: a:Reduce speed in the rain.,b:Keep tires properly inflated.,c:All of the above.,d:Ensure tires have good tread depth.
note: Prevent hydroplaning by reducing speed in wet conditions and maintaining proper tire pressure and tread depth.

question: Where do pedestrians have the right-of-way?
options: a:At an intersection crosswalk.,b:When crossing an alley or driveway.,c:If they are blind and using a cane or guide dog.,d:All of the above.
note: Pedestrians in crosswalks, crossing driveways/alleys, and blind pedestrians using aids have the right-of-way.

question: When preparing to turn left, drivers should:
options: a:Turn from any lane as long as the turn signal is on.,b:Speed up and cut in front of oncoming traffic.,c:Stop in the intersection before turning.,d:Signal in advance
note: Signal early, position in the left lane as appropriate, check for oncoming traffic and pedestrians, and slow smoothly before turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about speed is true?
options: a:Speeding can kill.,b:Speeding is safe if you are a skilled driver.,c:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
note: Both driving excessively fast and driving much slower than traffic can be dangerous; driving significantly below the flow of traffic on highways may cause unsafe passing maneuvers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you're waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection and opposing traffic blocks your view, what is the correct action?
options: a:Start the turn into only the first lane and complete it later.,b:Accelerate quickly when the first lane is clear.,c:Expect oncoming drivers to wave you through.,d:Wait until you can see all lanes you must cross before making the turn.
note: Do not begin the left turn until you have clear sight of all lanes you need to cross and can complete the maneuver safely.

question: If you hear a siren but cannot immediately see the emergency vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Keep driving until you see the vehicle.,b:Pull to the curb,c:Slow down but do not stop until you see it.
note: When you hear a siren, you must yield the right-of-way even if you cannot yet see the emergency vehicle. Safely move to the right side of the road and stop until you are sure the vehicle is not approaching your lane or direction of travel.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your freeway exit, what is the correct action?
options: a:Make a U-turn across the median.,b:Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit.,c:Continue to the next exit.,d:Cross several lanes at the last second to reach it.
note: If you miss your freeway exit, stay calm and continue driving to the next exit. Never stop, back up on the freeway, cross the median, or swerve across lanes at the last second, as these actions are illegal and extremely dangerous.

question: When is it permissible to park or stop on the shoulder of a freeway?
options: a:If you turn on your emergency flashers.,b:If no part of your vehicle is on the road.,c:To consult a map.,d:Only in an emergency.
note: On freeways, stopping or parking on the shoulder is generally prohibited except for emergencies, such as a breakdown, medical issue, or when directed by law enforcement. Simply being fully off the travel lane does not make it legal to stop there without an emergency.

question: How often does West Virginia require a state inspection of vehicles?
options: a:Only upon initial registration.,b:Every year.,c:Only if the vehicle is over 10 years old.,d:Every two years.
note: West Virginia requires most vehicles to pass a safety inspection once every year. Annual inspections help ensure that brakes, lights, tires, and other critical systems are in safe operating condition.

question: When meeting a vehicle with blinding headlights, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to pass quickly.,b:Flash your lights repeatedly.,c:Use your high beams until they dim theirs.,d:Look to the right side of the road to avoid being blinded.
note: When another vehicle’s headlights are blinding you, avoid looking directly at them. Instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane and use it as a guide until the vehicle passes. This reduces glare and helps you maintain your lane safely.

question: What is a potential penalty for a first DUI offense in West Virginia?
options: a:Three years in the state penitentiary and a $3 fine.,b:No penalties for first offense.,c:Possible jail time (up to six months depending on circumstances),d:Two months in county jail and a $30 fine.
note: For a first DUI offense in West Virginia, penalties can include fines, possible jail time up to six months depending on the circumstances, and driver’s license suspension. Penalties become more severe if there are aggravating factors such as high blood alcohol concentration, prior offenses, or causing injury or property damage.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a driver's left arm and hand are extended upward, what is the driver signaling?
options: a:Turning left.,b:Turning right.,c:Speeding up.,d:Stopping.
note: Standard hand signals are: left arm straight out for a left turn, left arm and hand extended upward for a right turn, and left arm and hand extended downward for slowing or stopping. A left arm raised up means the driver intends to turn right.

question: When must you yield to an emergency vehicle using lights or siren?
options: a:Only when other vehicles yield first.,b:Never,c:When you see flashing lights or hear a siren.,d:Only during daylight hours.
note: When you see flashing lights or hear a siren from an emergency vehicle approaching, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling as close as safely possible to the right edge of the road and stopping until the vehicle has passed, unless directed otherwise by law enforcement.

question: How is distracted driving characterized?
options: a:Very uncommon.,b:Not a safety concern.,c:Extremely risky behavior.,d:Only a problem for new drivers.
note: Distracted driving is extremely risky because it takes your attention away from the road, your hands off the wheel, or your mind off driving. Activities like texting, using a phone, eating, or adjusting controls greatly increase the chance of a crash for all drivers, not just new ones.

question: Are you ever allowed to drive around lowered railroad crossing gates?
options: a:If traffic is heavy and you are late for an appointment.,b:Under no circumstances.,c:When the train has passed and gates are still down.,d:When the lights stop flashing.
note: You must never drive around or under lowered railroad crossing gates, even if you do not see a train or think it has already passed. Trains can approach faster than they appear, and another train may be coming on a different track. Always wait until the gates are fully raised and warning signals have stopped before crossing.

question: Which of the following about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:You never need to stop at a crossing with a stop sign.,b:You may always drive around gates if no train is visible.,c:Crossings with gates are optional and may be ignored.,d:It is illegal to go around lowered gates
note: It is illegal and extremely dangerous to drive around lowered railroad crossing gates. Always stop when gates are down, red lights are flashing, or a flagger signals a train, and only proceed after the gates are fully raised and the tracks are clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection from different highways at the same time, who must yield?
options: a:The vehicle on the right must yield to the left.,b:Either vehicle may proceed with no yielding.,c:Yield only if one vehicle signals.,d:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This right‑of‑way rule helps prevent confusion and collisions when there are no signs or signals.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who must yield when a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light?
options: a:The pedestrian.,b:Whoever is slower.,c:Whoever started moving last.,d:The driver.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians who are legally crossing the street, even when there is no traffic light. When turning, slow down or stop as needed so pedestrians can cross safely before you complete your turn.

question: Compared with smaller cars, larger vehicles typically have:
options: a:No blind spots due to mirrors.,b:Smaller blind spots than compact cars.,c:Automatic sensors that eliminate blind spots.,d:Much larger blind spots.
note: Large vehicles such as trucks and buses have much larger blind spots than smaller cars. These blind areas exist along the sides, directly behind, and sometimes in front of the vehicle, so you should avoid driving in those areas where the driver may not see you.

question: What does an \End school zone sign indicate?"
options: a:That a crosswalk is ahead.,b:That the speed limit is 20 mph.,c:The start of a reduced-speed school zone.,d:The end of the reduced school-zone speed limit.
note: An “End School Zone” sign tells you that the special reduced speed limit for the school zone is no longer in effect. After passing this sign, you may resume the regular posted speed for that roadway, as long as conditions are safe.

question: What should be your first response to reduced visibility while driving?
options: a:Turn on high-beam headlights.,b:Turn on windshield wipers.,c:Stop immediately in the travel lane.,d:Reduce your speed.
note: Reducing your speed is the safest first response when visibility drops. Slowing down gives you more time to see hazards and react. After slowing, you can take other steps as needed, such as turning on appropriate lights or wipers, but your immediate action should be to reduce speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when you come to an intersection displaying a flashing red light?
options: a:Wait for a flashing green light.,b:Ignore it and continue driving normally.,c:Come to a full stop,d:Slow and pass through if clear.
note: A flashing red light is treated the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, and then proceed only when it is safe. You cannot just slow down and roll through the intersection.

question: Your vehicle's stopping distance becomes longer when you are stopping:
options: a:On dry paved highways.,b:When driving at night under clear conditions.,c:When your vehicle is unloaded and light.,d:On wet or icy pavement.
note: On wet or icy pavement, your tires have less traction, so it takes much longer to stop. You should increase your following distance and slow down in these conditions to allow enough space to stop safely.

question: What should you do when driving in foggy conditions?
options: a:Turn on your high beam headlights.,b:Drive at the maximum speed limit.,c:Turn on your low beam headlights.,d:Turn on your hazard lights.
note: In fog, always use low-beam headlights. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see. With low beams on, slow down and increase your following distance so you have more time to react to hazards you may not see until you are closer.

question: What does an orange-colored traffic sign typically indicate?
options: a:The start of a no-passing zone.,b:Construction or maintenance ahead.,c:A hospital nearby.,d:A school zone ahead.
note: Orange traffic signs are used for construction, maintenance, and work zones. They warn you to be prepared for workers, equipment, lane shifts, or reduced speeds, and to use extra caution when driving through these areas.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic in opposite directions, when should you return to your lane?
options: a:When a passing zone ends.,b:Only after signaling for five seconds.,c:When there's enough room between you and the passed vehicle.,d:Immediately after passing regardless of distance.
note: After you pass on a two-lane road, stay in the left lane until you can see the entire front of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror and there is a safe gap ahead. Then signal, check your blind spot, and return to your lane smoothly without cutting back in too closely.

question: Lack of sleep affects driving ability similarly to which of the following?
options: a:The effect that amphetamines have.,b:The effect that anger has.,c:The effect that alcohol has.,d:The effect that caffeine has.
note: Fatigue affects your driving in many of the same ways as alcohol: it slows reaction time, reduces awareness, and impairs judgment and coordination. Being awake for long periods can impair you to a level similar to having alcohol in your system, which is why drowsy driving is so dangerous.

question: When driving in rain, you must use which headlights?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Parking lights only.,c:No lights are necessary in daylight rain.,d:Low beam headlights.
note: In rain, always use low beam headlights. Low beams make your vehicle more visible and reduce glare reflected from rain, fog, or mist. High beams can reflect off moisture in the air and on the road, making it harder for you and other drivers to see.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should a driver who is traveling much slower than the normal flow of traffic do?
options: a:Refuse to allow cars to pass behind them.,b:Accelerate to the speed limit regardless of conditions.,c:Pull off the road at the earliest safe point to let traffic pass if it is causing a backup.,d:Always stay in the left lane.
note: If you are driving much slower than the normal flow and causing a line of vehicles behind you, especially on a two-lane road, you should pull off at the first safe turnout or wide shoulder to let traffic pass. This reduces driver frustration and lowers the risk of unsafe passing maneuvers.

question: A telltale sign of a drunk driver often includes:
options: a:Driving steadily at the speed limit.,b:Weaving between lanes.,c:Carefully signaling every move.,d:Always obeying traffic laws.
note: A common sign of an impaired or drunk driver is weaving or drifting between lanes. Other warning signs include driving much too slowly or too fast, sudden lane changes, inconsistent speeds, and abrupt or inappropriate braking.

question: What is the most important speed-management rule for navigating curves?
options: a:Slow down before entering the curve so inertia doesn't push you outward.,b:Speed up before the curve and brake in the sharpest part.,c:Maintain posted speed and brake hard mid-curve.,d:Use engine braking only while in the curve.
note: Reducing speed before entering a curve is essential because your vehicle’s inertia wants to keep moving straight. If you enter too fast, this outward force can cause you to skid or run off the road. Slow down before the curve, then maintain a safe, steady speed through it and avoid hard braking while turning whenever possible.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing and you do not see or hear a train, you must stop if:
options: a:Never,b:A stop sign is posted or crossing lights are flashing or gates are lowered.,c:Only if a train is visible.,d:Only if a flagger is present.
note: At railroad crossings, you must stop when the red lights are flashing, the gate is down or coming down, a stop sign is posted, or any official signal or flagger directs you to stop. Even if you do not see or hear a train, these controls mean a train may be approaching and you must remain stopped until it is safe to proceed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red light on a traffic signal means:
options: a:The traffic signal is broken so you may proceed as usual.,b:You do not have to stop if no other cars are present.,c:You must slow but not stop.,d:The same as a stop sign — come to a complete stop
note: A flashing red traffic signal is treated exactly like a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop at the limit line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, then proceed only when it is safe and after yielding to any pedestrians or vehicles with the right-of-way.

question: In cold or wet weather, which road sections freeze more quickly and stay icy longer?
options: a:Flat open areas exposed to the sun.,b:Shaded areas (sections of road shaded by trees or buildings).,c:Curvy sections of road.,d:Roads with many streetlights.
note: Shaded areas of the road, such as those under trees, bridges, or next to buildings, freeze sooner and stay icy longer because they receive less sunlight. Even when the rest of the road looks clear, these spots can remain slick, so reduce speed and use extra caution when driving through shaded sections in cold or wet weather.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your turn or exit on a freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Make a quick U-turn.,b:Continue to the next exit or safe turnaround.,c:Cut across lanes to return to the exit.,d:Stop and back up on the shoulder.
note: If you miss your exit on a freeway, you must never stop, back up, or make a U-turn on the freeway or shoulder. Continue driving to the next exit or another safe place where you can legally turn around. Backing up or cutting across lanes is extremely dangerous and illegal on high-speed roads.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light require you to do?
options: a:Stop and wait for a green light.,b:Proceed with caution.,c:Speed up to clear the intersection.,d:Yield only to pedestrians.
note: A flashing yellow light means you do not have to stop, but you must slow down and proceed carefully. Look for cross traffic, pedestrians, or other hazards and be prepared to yield if necessary.

question: When a school bus is stopped with its red lights flashing, you must stop from both directions at what approximate distance?
options: a:You must stop before reaching the bus and remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the bus moves or the driver signals you to proceed.,b:Within 50 feet of the bus.,c:Within 30 feet of the bus.,d:Within 10 feet of the bus.
note: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, drivers in both directions (unless on a divided highway where your side is separated by a median) must stop before reaching the bus and remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the bus moves or the driver signals you to proceed. The law is based on stopping, not on being a specific number of feet from the bus.

question: If your power steering fails while driving, you should:
options: a:Turn off the ignition immediately while moving.,b:Brake hard and shift into neutral immediately.,c:Work harder to steer and gradually slow down to pull off the road safely.,d:Honk and continue at the same speed to the nearest exit.
note: If power steering fails, the steering wheel will be much harder to turn, but you can still steer the vehicle. Grip the wheel firmly, steer with extra effort, and gradually slow down and move to a safe place off the road. Do not turn off the ignition while moving, because that can lock the steering wheel.

question: While waiting in the intersection to complete a left turn, how should you position your wheels?
options: a:Turn your wheels sharply to the left so you can complete the turn quickly.,b:Flash your headlights to alert other drivers.,c:Turn your wheels to the right as a precaution.,d:Keep your wheels straight while signaling and waiting.
note: When waiting in an intersection to turn left, keep your wheels pointed straight. If another vehicle hits you from behind while your wheels are turned left, your car could be pushed into oncoming traffic. Keeping the wheels straight lets you go forward instead of into opposing lanes if you are struck.

question: Signs indicating areas of public recreation typically have which color?
options: a:Green.,b:Orange.,c:Red.,d:Brown.
note: Brown traffic signs are used for recreational and cultural interest areas, such as parks, campgrounds, and historic sites. This helps drivers quickly recognize locations related to outdoor activities and points of interest.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection simultaneously, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.,b:The largest vehicle has the right-of-way.,c:The car on the left has the right-of-way.,d:The vehicle that honks first has the right-of-way.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This means the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

question: If you are taking a non-prescription drug, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Read the labels for warnings about driving and side effects.,b:Drink alcohol instead to counteract side effects.,c:Ignore label warnings if you feel fine.,d:Double the dose to build tolerance.
note: Many over-the-counter medicines can make you drowsy, dizzy, or otherwise impair your driving. Always read the label for warnings about driving or operating machinery, and if you are unsure, ask a doctor or pharmacist before you drive.

question: A single broken white line down the center of a two-lane road indicates:
options: a:Lanes moving in the same direction where passing is not allowed.,b:Lanes moving in the same direction that may be crossed to pass when safe.,c:Lanes moving in opposite directions where passing is prohibited.,d:A no-passing zone.
note: A single broken (dashed) white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross it to change lanes or pass when it is safe and legal to do so.

question: What is the first adjustment you should make when getting into a car to drive?
options: a:Adjust your seat to a comfortable and safe driving position.,b:Buckle your seat belt after moving the seat.,c:Adjust the steering wheel before the seat.,d:Adjust the radio to a low volume.
note: When you get into the driver’s seat, adjust the seat first so you can comfortably reach the pedals, steering wheel, and controls and see clearly out of the windows. After that, adjust mirrors, steering wheel, and then fasten your seat belt.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must not drive at a speed greater than:
options: a:The posted maximum speed limit.,b:A speed that is reasonable and prudent for conditions (which may be lower than the posted limit).,c:A speed the driver prefers.,d:A speed that shortcuts traffic.
note: You must never drive faster than the posted maximum speed limit, and you must also slow down below that limit when conditions (rain, traffic, visibility, road surface) require it. The speed limit is an absolute maximum, not a target speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you behave when a funeral procession approaches an intersection you are waiting at?
options: a:Expect the procession to yield to you.,b:Yield to the procession after the lead vehicle crosses the intersection.,c:Try to beat the lead vehicle through the intersection.
note: In many states, funeral processions have the right of way once the lead vehicle lawfully enters the intersection. You should remain stopped and allow the entire procession to pass, rather than trying to cut through it. Yielding after the lead vehicle enters the intersection is both courteous and often required by law.

question: When preparing to change lanes, what checks should you perform?
options: a:Quickly turn your head without using mirrors.,b:Only check your rearview mirror.,c:Sound your horn before moving.,d:Check your side and rearview mirrors and briefly check your blind spot over your shoulder.
note: Before changing lanes, you must use a three-step check: first check your mirrors to see traffic behind and beside you, then quickly look over your shoulder in the direction of the lane change to check your blind spot, and signal and move only when it is safe. Relying only on mirrors or only turning your head without using mirrors is unsafe.

question: What causes 'highway hypnosis'?
options: a:Staring at the roadway for long periods and failing to actively scan.,b:Frequent rest stops during a long trip.,c:Getting too much sleep the night before driving.
note: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare straight ahead for long periods without actively scanning your surroundings. Your mind can drift, and you may not remember parts of the drive. To prevent this, move your eyes regularly, take breaks, and stay mentally engaged with the driving task.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another motorist is trying to pass your vehicle, what is the correct action?
options: a:Signal when you want the other driver to pass.,b:Pull off the road immediately.,c:Stay in your lane and maintain or slightly reduce your speed to allow safe passing.
note: When another driver is passing you, stay in your lane and maintain a steady speed or slightly reduce speed to help them pass safely. Do not speed up or move onto the shoulder. You do not need to check for oncoming traffic for them; your main job is to hold a predictable path and speed so they can judge the pass safely.

question: What does a solid yellow line beside your lane signify?
options: a:Slow down.,b:Do not pass.,c:Pass with caution.
note: A solid yellow line next to your lane means you must not pass vehicles traveling in your direction at that location. It marks a no-passing zone for your side of the road, usually because of limited visibility or other hazards.

question: Which is important for safe night driving?
options: a:Never drive if you are tired.,b:Ensure your headlights work.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: At night your ability to see hazards is reduced, so increasing your following distance is especially important. Leaving more space gives you extra time to react if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly. You should also be sure your headlights work properly and avoid driving when tired, but increasing following distance is a key night‑driving safety practice.

question: Why must drivers take care when passing bicyclists?
options: a:Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass.,b:The bicycle always has the right-of-way.,c:You are moving faster than the bicycle.
note: When passing bicyclists, you must leave plenty of space because they may need to swerve around potholes or debris, and oncoming drivers may not see you move into the opposing lane to pass. This combination makes passing riskier, so you must check carefully for oncoming traffic and only pass when it is clearly safe. Bicycles do not always have the right‑of‑way, and simply being faster than a bicycle is not the main safety concern.

question: Why must drivers be more careful at night?
options: a:Traffic moves faster at night.,b:There is more traffic at night.,c:Drivers cannot see as well at night.
note: At night you cannot see as far or as clearly as during the day, even with headlights. This reduced visibility makes it harder to spot pedestrians, animals, and hazards in time to react safely. Because you see less, you must drive more carefully, use your headlights properly, and adjust your speed and following distance. Traffic is not always faster or heavier at night, but visibility is always reduced.

question: Why should you avoid following too closely behind another vehicle?
options: a:You may not see the road between the cars.,b:You might not have time to stop if the car ahead brakes suddenly.,c:You may miss the vehicle's turn signals.,d:It helps you travel faster.
note: Following too closely, or tailgating, leaves you little time and space to react if the vehicle ahead brakes or stops suddenly. You need enough following distance to see what is happening ahead and to stop smoothly without hitting the car in front of you. Keeping a safe following distance is a core defensive‑driving habit that helps prevent rear‑end collisions.

question: Which recommendation does NOT promote safe night driving?
options: a:Having heavily tinted windows that reduce visibility at night is safe.,b:Keep the windshield clean to reduce glare.,c:Carry a flashlight in the vehicle for emergencies.,d:Be aware that tinted windows can reduce darkness visibility.
note: Heavily tinted windows reduce how much you can see at night, especially in low‑light areas, and can make it harder to spot pedestrians, cyclists, and hazards. For safe night driving, keep your windshield clean to reduce glare, understand that any tint can reduce visibility in darkness, and carry a flashlight for emergencies outside the vehicle. Avoid dark tints that limit your night vision and may violate state tint laws.

question: Which practice can help reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
options: a:Refuse to use turn signals so others adapt.,b:Tailgate slower drivers to keep traffic moving.,c:Speed up to pass slower drivers quickly.,d:Allow extra travel time so you are not rushed.
note: Allowing extra travel time reduces the urge to rush, speed, tailgate, or make risky maneuvers. Planning ahead and not being in a hurry helps you stay calm, signal properly, and follow at safe distances, which lowers the chance of road rage and aggressive driving.
