question: What does an octagonal (eight-sided) traffic sign always indicate?
options: a:Speed limit sign.,b:Hospital sign.,c:Stop sign.,d:Yield sign.
note: In the U.S., the octagon shape is used only for STOP signs. When you see an eight‑sided sign, you must come to a complete stop at the limit line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, and then proceed only when it is safe.

question: To help relieve fatigue on a long trip, which practice is recommended?
options: a:Drive continuously and only stop for fuel every five hours.,b:Keep driving but sip strong coffee.,c:Open a window and drive with music loud.,d:Stop for a rest every two hours or sooner if drowsy.
note: On long trips, you should stop to rest about every two hours, and sooner if you feel drowsy. Short breaks, stretching, or a brief nap in a safe place are far more effective and safer than relying on coffee, loud music, or open windows to fight fatigue.

question: A flashing red traffic signal requires drivers to:
options: a:Stop and then proceed when the way is clear, just like a stop sign.,b:Slow down but not stop.,c:Yield only to vehicles from the right.,d:Proceed as if it's a green light.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. Stop at the limit line or before the crosswalk, check for traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when the way is clear.

question: If you leave your vehicle unattended, you must:
options: a:Turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.,b:Leave the engine running to keep accessories on.,c:Leave the key in the ignition for a short errand.,d:Only lock the doors without removing the key.
note: When leaving a vehicle unattended, turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a posted speed limit represent?
options: a:The speed you must always drive regardless of conditions.,b:The maximum legal speed you can travel under dangerous conditions.,c:The maximum or minimum legal speed under ideal conditions.,d:A suggested safe speed for wet conditions.
note: A posted speed limit shows the fastest (and sometimes slowest) speed allowed in ideal conditions. You must slow down below the limit when conditions are poor, such as in rain, fog, heavy traffic, or on damaged roads.

question: Why is night driving more difficult than daytime driving?
options: a:It is always raining at night.,b:Visibility is reduced in the dark,c:There are more pedestrians at night than day.,d:Cars overheat more quickly at night.
note: At night, your headlights limit how far you can see, and your eyes do not see as well in the dark. This reduced visibility makes it harder to spot hazards in time, so you must use headlights correctly and adjust your speed and following distance.

question: A regulatory sign with a red circle and slash through a symbol indicates:
options: a:An action is forbidden.,b:Drivers should come to a complete stop.,c:Some drivers must yield to others.,d:That the road is closed.
note: A regulatory sign with a red circle and a diagonal slash over a symbol means that the pictured action is not allowed. For example, a right-turn arrow with a red slash means no right turn at that location.

question: Which factor greatly affects your ability to stop?
options: a:The time of day only.,b:Road conditions,c:The number of passengers in the car.,d:The color of your vehicle.
note: Road conditions—such as wet, icy, gravel, or uneven surfaces—have a major impact on how quickly you can stop. On poor surfaces, your tires have less traction, so you must slow down and increase following distance to stop safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when a traffic signal turns green?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.,b:Accelerate as quickly as possible.,c:Back up slowly.,d:Proceed if the intersection is clear, yielding to pedestrians and any traffic still in the intersection.
note: When a traffic signal turns green, you may proceed only after yielding to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to any vehicles still in the intersection. Always check that the intersection is clear before moving, even when you have a green light.

question: Of the following, which is hardest to see at night?
options: a:Pedestrians.,b:Road signs.,c:Other motorists.,d:Streetlights.
note: Pedestrians are unlit, often wear dark clothing, and move unpredictably, so they are much harder to see at night than reflective road signs, vehicle headlights/taillights, or fixed streetlights. Always scan carefully for people walking along or crossing the road in low‑light conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it safe to pass on a two-way, two-lane road?
options: a:When you can clearly see the road ahead.,b:Only if all three of the above are true.,c:When your vehicle can reach the speed required to pass.,d:When you can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.
note: On a two‑way, two‑lane road, you may only pass when all safety conditions are met: you can clearly see the road ahead, your vehicle can accelerate and complete the pass safely, and you can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic. If any of these are not true, you must not pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?
options: a:Only when traffic is heavy.,b:Only if the vehicle is small.,c:Just after you start passing.,d:Early enough that other drivers know your intent.
note: You should always signal well in advance of changing lanes or passing so other drivers have time to see your signal and adjust. Signaling early makes your intentions clear and reduces the chance of conflicts or sudden braking.

question: Drivers who have consumed alcohol before driving:
options: a:Are better drivers because they are more careful.,b:Have faster reaction times than sober drivers.,c:Do not have sufficient control over their bodies,d:Are always aware of the risks they are taking.
note: Alcohol slows reaction time and harms judgment, coordination, and vision. Even small amounts reduce your ability to control the vehicle safely, so you do not have sufficient control over your body or driving decisions after drinking.

question: When driving on potentially slippery roads, you should:
options: a:Use cruise control to keep a constant speed.,b:Always drive at the maximum posted speed.,c:Increase your following distance and avoid sudden speed changes.,d:Make abrupt steering corrections to stay in lane.
note: On slippery roads you should slow down, avoid sudden acceleration, braking, or steering, and increase your following distance to give yourself more time to react. Reducing your following distance is unsafe on slick surfaces because you need extra space to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On an interstate, before changing lanes you should:
options: a:Stop on the shoulder if tired.,b:Always use cruise control.,c:Signal.,d:Change lanes frequently to stay alert.
note: Before changing lanes on an interstate, you must always signal to let other drivers know your intention. Then check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to check blind spots before moving. Cruise control is optional and not required for lane changes.

question: Pentagonal signs are used to indicate:
options: a:Speed limits.,b:Pedestrian-only areas.,c:No passing zones.,d:School zones and school crossings.
note: Pentagonal (five-sided) signs are used for school zones and school crossings. When you see this shape, slow down, watch for children, and be prepared to stop for pedestrians in or near the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady yellow arrow indicate?
options: a:Slow and stop if safe to do so.,b:You may turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic.,c:Merge into the lane indicated by the arrow.
note: A steady yellow arrow means the protected turning movement is ending and a red arrow is about to appear. You should slow down and stop if it is safe to do so. If you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely, you may complete the turn with caution.

question: If you must stop along the road at night, what lights should be used?
options: a:Turn off all lights to conserve battery.,b:Use high beams to warn others.,c:Use your emergency flashers and keep your low-beam headlights on so others can see you.,d:Use only parking lights.
note: If you must stop along the road at night, turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low-beam headlights on so other drivers can see you. High beams can blind approaching drivers, and turning off all lights or using only parking lights makes your vehicle hard to see.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a vehicle is tailgating you, what should you do?
options: a:If no right lane exists, wait until the road ahead is clear and gradually slow to encourage them to pass.,b:Immediately slow down abruptly to warn them.,c:Sound your horn and stay in your lane.,d:Move into the right lane if one is available.
note: If a vehicle is tailgating you, the safest response is to increase your following distance ahead and, when possible, move into the right lane so the other driver can pass. If there is no right lane, wait until the road ahead is clear and gradually reduce speed so they can pass safely. Never brake suddenly, as this can cause a rear-end collision.

question: If another car is about to hit you, what action should you take to warn them?
options: a:Shout from inside your vehicle.,b:Turn on your emergency flashers only.,c:Wave your arms out the window.,d:Sound your horn to alert the other driver or pedestrian.
note: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians when they may not see you and a collision could occur. Shouting, waving, or relying only on emergency flashers is ineffective in an immediate hazard; the horn is designed to quickly get others’ attention.

question: Signs that require drivers to obey an instruction are called:
options: a:Information signs.,b:Guide signs.,c:Regulatory signs.,d:Warning signs.
note: Regulatory signs tell you about laws and rules you must obey, such as speed limit, stop, yield, and no parking signs. Ignoring a regulatory sign can result in a traffic violation. Guide and information signs provide directions or information, and warning signs alert you to hazards, but they are not commands in the same way regulatory signs are.

question: If another driver cuts you off, the best reaction is to:
options: a:Let it go and continue driving safely.,b:Flash your high beams and chase them.,c:Pull up beside them and shout.,d:Brake-check them to teach a lesson.
note: If another driver cuts you off, stay calm, create space, and continue driving safely. Do not respond with aggressive actions like chasing, brake-checking, or yelling, as these can escalate into road rage and increase the risk of a crash. Let the incident go and focus on defensive driving.

question: How can stress affect your driving performance?
options: a:It will make you fall asleep at the wheel.,b:It improves your reaction time.,c:It can reduce your ability to concentrate and impair driving judgment.,d:It decreases your chances of an accident.
note: Stress and strong emotions can distract you, slow your reactions, and impair your judgment, making it harder to notice hazards and make safe decisions. When you are very upset, angry, or stressed, it is safer to delay driving or take time to calm down before getting behind the wheel.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before turning left, what is an important right-of-way consideration?
options: a:Cut across lanes to get into position quickly.,b:Yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians before completing the turn.,c:Sound your horn to warn others.,d:Swing to the right side of your lane to prepare.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming vehicles that are close enough to be a hazard and to pedestrians in the crosswalk. Wait until there is a safe gap in traffic and the crosswalk is clear before completing your turn, even if you have a green light.

question: On a divided multilane highway when you hear or see an approaching emergency vehicle, you should:
options: a:Slow down.,b:Speed up to clear the lane.,c:Move safely to the side and stop to give a clear path.,d:Disregard the signal if other lanes exist.
note: On a divided multilane highway, you must yield the right-of-way to emergency vehicles using sirens or flashing lights. Do not just stop where you are if it would block their path. Instead, safely move to the right side of your lane or roadway and stop, or otherwise position your vehicle so the emergency vehicle has a clear path. Always use your mirrors and signals and avoid sudden stops that could cause a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From which lane should you begin a left turn from a multilane one-way street?
options: a:The right lane.,b:The left-most lane.,c:Either lane is acceptable.,d:The center lane.
note: When turning left from a multilane one-way street, you should begin the turn from the left-most lane unless signs or lane markings indicate otherwise. Starting from the left lane positions you closest to the center of the intersection and reduces conflicts with traffic going straight or turning right.

question: What is the act of turning your head to check blind spots before changing lanes called?
options: a:A bad driving habit.,b:A good driving habit and necessary for safe lane changes.,c:An illegal maneuver.,d:Unnecessary if you have mirrors.
note: Turning your head briefly to check your blind spots before changing lanes is called making a head check and is a necessary safe driving habit. Mirrors do not show areas directly alongside and slightly behind your vehicle, so you must glance over your shoulder to be sure the lane is clear before moving over.

question: Which is a safe technique for driving through a curve?
options: a:Maintain the exact same speed throughout regardless of curve severity.,b:Slow down before entering the curve and accelerate gradually as you exit.,c:Speed up before entering and slow down while exiting.,d:Brake hard in the middle of the curve to stay controlled.
note: For safe curve driving, slow down before you enter the curve so your speed is under control as you turn. Once you are past the sharpest part of the curve and your vehicle is stable, you can gradually accelerate as you exit. Braking hard in the curve or entering too fast can cause skidding or loss of control.

question: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children, what should you do before proceeding?
options: a:Proceed as soon as the bus door closes regardless of children.,b:Accelerate quickly to pass the bus.,c:Watch carefully for children walking along the side of the road before moving.,d:Honk to alert children to move aside.
note: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children, remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn. Before you proceed, carefully check all sides of the road and around the bus for children who may be crossing or walking near traffic. Children can be unpredictable, so move forward slowly and be prepared to stop again.

question: What should you never do while stopped in a travel lane?
options: a:Stop to drop off passengers.,b:Stop to look up an address.,c:Make a U-turn or back up if you missed an exit.,d:All of the above.
note: You must not stop in a travel lane for non-emergencies. Stopping to drop off passengers, look up an address, or make a U-turn/back up after missing an exit all create a serious hazard. If you miss an exit, continue to the next safe place to turn around rather than stopping or reversing in the lane.

question: Which substances can impair driving and lead to DUII charges?
options: a:Beer.,b:Illegal drugs and certain prescription medications.,c:Inhalants like glue or paint.,d:All of the above.
note: Any substance that impairs your ability to drive safely can lead to a DUI or similar impaired-driving charge. This includes alcoholic drinks like beer, illegal drugs, many prescription medications that affect alertness or coordination, and inhalants such as glue or paint fumes. You are responsible for knowing how what you take affects your driving.

question: Guide signs that show directions and mileage typically have what color background?
options: a:Red.,b:Blue.,c:Yellow.,d:Green.
note: Destination and distance guide signs are typically green with white lettering. They show directions to cities, streets, and highways and give mileage information so you can plan lane changes and turns in advance.

question: What is the typical effect of driving while distracted?
options: a:It is never dangerous.,b:It usually causes the driver to react more slowly to hazards.,c:It usually causes the driver to drive faster.
note: Distractions such as phone use, eating, or adjusting controls take your eyes, mind, or hands away from driving. This usually slows your reaction time, so you notice hazards later and have less time and space to avoid them, greatly increasing your crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who must you yield to when entering a roundabout?
options: a:Pedestrians only.,b:Bicyclists inside the roundabout only.,c:Vehicles already in the roundabout.
note: When approaching a roundabout, you must yield to traffic already circulating in the roundabout and to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing the entry or exit lanes. Wait for a safe gap before entering, and always give the right of way to people in the crosswalks.

question: What usually causes hydroplaning?
options: a:Excessive speed on wet surfaces.,b:Sudden turns.,c:Walking on the road.,d:Overuse of brakes.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride up on a thin layer of water and lose contact with the road. This is most likely at higher speeds on wet pavement, especially with under‑inflated or worn tires. The faster you drive on a wet surface, the harder it is for the tire treads to channel water away, increasing the risk of hydroplaning.

question: What is the illegal minimum blood alcohol concentration (BAC) for drivers age 21 or older in West Virginia?
options: a:0.08 percent.,b:0.05 percent.,c:0.10 percent.,d:0.02 percent.
note: For drivers age 21 and older in West Virginia, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher. At 0.08% BAC, you are considered legally impaired and can be arrested for DUI. Lower limits apply to commercial drivers and drivers under 21, but 0.08% is the standard adult per se limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The space you need to cross oncoming traffic safely depends on:
options: a:Road and weather conditions and the amount of oncoming traffic.,b:Whether you used your turn signal.,c:The color of your vehicle.,d:The presence of a crosswalk only.
note: The time and space you need to cross oncoming traffic safely depend on how fast other vehicles are coming, how many there are, and the road and weather conditions. Wet, icy, or gravel roads and poor visibility all mean you need more time and distance to cross safely.

question: When parked facing downhill, how should your front wheels be turned?
options: a:Turned away from the curb.,b:Turned partially toward the center of the road.,c:Aiming straight ahead.,d:Turned toward the curb.
note: When you park facing downhill with a curb, turn the front wheels toward the curb and set the parking brake. If the vehicle starts to roll, the front tire will roll gently into the curb and stop the car instead of letting it roll into traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When the traffic light turns from green to yellow as you approach an intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to beat the red.,b:Stop in the center of the intersection.,c:Apply brakes sharply to stop immediately.,d:Prepare to stop safely unless already in the intersection.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. You should slow down and prepare to stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection or too close to stop safely, continue through with caution rather than speeding up.

question: How serious is drinking alcohol and driving?
options: a:A minor traffic safety problem.,b:A serious traffic safety problem.,c:Safe if only a few drinks are consumed.,d:Only an issue for inexperienced drivers.
note: Driving after drinking is a serious safety hazard and significantly raises the likelihood of crashes and injuries.

question: What do double solid yellow lines in the center of the road mean?
options: a:Passing is permitted for both directions.,b:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,c:You must stop before proceeding.,d:One-way traffic ahead.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate opposite directions and prohibit passing from either side except in limited turning situations.

question: When must you pull over and allow an emergency vehicle to pass?
options: a:Only if it is following you.,b:Only if it is approaching from the opposite direction.,c:Regardless of the direction it's coming from.,d:Only if it has a siren but no lights.
note: You must pull over to the right edge and stop for emergency vehicles with flashing lights or sirens regardless of their direction.

question: If a vehicle with Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) begins to lose traction, what should the driver do?
options: a:Switch off the ABS system immediately.,b:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly and steer out of danger,c:Pump the brakes rapidly to simulate ABS.,d:Release the brake and then reapply it repeatedly.
note: With ABS, press and hold the brake; the system will modulate braking automatically while you steer to safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a stop sign, what is the correct visual check order before proceeding?
options: a:Check the rearview mirror.,b:Look right first.,c:Look left first, then right, then left again before proceeding.,d:Move when the vehicle ahead moves.
note: At a stop sign, you must come to a complete stop and scan for traffic. Look left first because vehicles from the left are closer to you and will reach the intersection sooner. Then look right for approaching traffic or pedestrians, and finally look left again before moving to be sure it is still clear. This left–right–left pattern helps you detect any new hazards that may have appeared.

question: A steady green traffic light means:
options: a:You must stop and look for a green arrow.,b:You must slow and prepare to stop.,c:You may proceed through the intersection if the road is clear.,d:You may only turn right.
note: A steady green light means you may go straight or turn, but only if the intersection is clear and it is safe. You must still yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to oncoming traffic when turning left.

question: Seat belts are most effective when worn by:
options: a:Just front-seat occupants during the day.,b:All occupants of the vehicle,c:Only passengers on long trips.,d:Only the driver.
note: Seat belts work best when everyone in the vehicle is properly restrained. In a crash, unbelted passengers can be seriously injured and can also injure others in the vehicle.

question: What is meant by the term 'No zone' around large trucks or buses?
options: a:A roadway with restrictions on vehicle stereo volume.,b:A term used to describe blind spots around a truck or bus.,c:A special speed zone.
note: The 'No zone' is the large blind-spot area around trucks and buses where the driver cannot see you. Avoid driving for long periods directly beside, behind, or very close in front of large vehicles.

question: Which of the following is true about seat belts and child restraints?
options: a:Seat belts are unnecessary for short trips.,b:Never place a rear-facing infant seat in a front seat with an active passenger airbag.,c:Children 12 and under should always sit in the front seat.,d:Airbags are always safe for infants and small children.
note: Rear-facing infant seats must never be placed in front of an active airbag because the airbag can seriously injure or kill the child. Children are safest properly restrained in the back seat, especially those 12 and under.

question: What do your brake lights communicate to other drivers?
options: a:You are making a turn.,b:You are slowing down or stopping.,c:You are changing lanes.,d:You have your emergency brake on.
note: Brake lights warn drivers behind you that you are slowing down or stopping. This gives them time to reduce speed and maintain a safe following distance, helping to prevent rear-end collisions.

question: When should you look over your shoulder to check your vehicle's blind spot?
options: a:Every five minutes while driving.,b:Only on highways when passing another vehicle.,c:Only when parking.,d:Whenever you are changing lanes
note: Blind spots are areas you cannot see with your mirrors alone. Any time you change the position of your vehicle sideways—such as changing lanes, merging, or pulling away from the curb—you must quickly look over your shoulder to check your blind spot in addition to using your mirrors.

question: When preparing to change lanes, what important actions should you take?
options: a:Signal early, check your blind spot, and ensure the lane is clear before entering.,b:Signal only as you start the lane change.,c:Make rapid lane changes to minimize time in adjacent lanes.,d:Turn your headlights on to warn other drivers.
note: Before changing lanes, signal well in advance to alert other drivers, check your mirrors, then quickly look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Only move into the new lane when you are sure it is clear and safe, and change lanes smoothly without sudden swerves.

question: When driving in fog, which of the following should you do?
options: a:Turn on hazard lights and increase speed.,b:Follow the vehicle ahead closely.,c:Use high beam headlights for better illumination.,d:Drive cautiously
note: In fog, you should slow down, increase your following distance, and drive cautiously using low beam headlights. High beams reflect off the fog and can make it harder to see, while low beams and, if equipped, fog lights help you see the road and be seen by others more safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the proper action if you miss your interstate exit?
options: a:Quickly cross lanes to make the exit.,b:Make a U-turn to return to the exit.,c:Continue to the next exit and leave there.
note: If you miss your exit on an interstate, keep going to the next exit. Do not stop, back up on the ramp or shoulder, or make a U‑turn on the highway. Continue to the next safe exit, then follow signs or directions to get back to your intended route.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Passing is prohibited in which locations?
options: a:Only in school zones.,b:On hills,c:Only on multi-lane highways.,d:Only when signs say no passing.
note: Passing is especially dangerous and typically prohibited where you cannot see far enough ahead, such as on hills and curves, and also at intersections, railroad crossings, and in marked no‑passing zones. On hills, your view of oncoming traffic is blocked, so you must not cross the center line to pass.

question: You should drive below the posted speed limit when:
options: a:Anything makes road conditions less than perfect (wet, slippery, poor visibility).,b:You see a police car only.,c:You are entering a highway with other cars.,d:Traffic is flowing faster than the limit.
note: You must adjust your speed to match conditions, not just the posted limit. When the road is wet, icy, covered with snow, or visibility is reduced by fog, rain, or darkness, you are required to slow down below the posted speed so you can stop safely and maintain control.

question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is traveling in your area, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to create distance.,b:Stop immediately in your lane.,c:Make every effort to give the emergency vehicle a clear path of travel.,d:Maintain your speed and lane.
note: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights and siren approaches, you must yield the right-of-way. Safely move to the right side of the road and stop, or otherwise clear a path so the vehicle can pass quickly and safely. Do not speed up or stop in the middle of your lane in a way that blocks its route.

question: If involved in a crash, what should a driver do at the scene?
options: a:Stop at or near the scene and move out of traffic if possible.,b:Stand or walk in traffic lanes to direct cars.,c:Leave without leaving information.,d:Drive away slowly and report later.
note: If you are involved in a crash, you must stop at or near the scene and, if possible, move your vehicle out of traffic to a safe place. Check for injuries, call emergency services, and exchange information. Do not stand in traffic lanes, and never leave the scene without providing required information.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before and after passing another vehicle?
options: a:Check your mirrors and blind spots before changing lanes to pass and again before returning to your lane.,b:Sound your horn three times.,c:Move back into the lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.
note: Safe passing requires checking your mirrors and blind spots before moving into the passing lane and again before returning to your original lane. Signal before changing lanes, pass promptly, and only move back when you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror with a safe following distance.

question: What color lines divide lanes of traffic moving in the same direction?
options: a:Red.,b:Yellow.,c:Blue.,d:White.
note: White lane lines separate traffic moving in the same direction, such as multiple lanes on a one-way street or freeway. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Knowing this helps you understand when passing is allowed and which side of the road you should be on.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing warning sign, you should:
options: a:Drive faster than the train.,b:Look for a way around lowered gates.,c:Ignore it if no train is visible.,d:Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby.
note: Railroad warning signs mean you are approaching tracks where trains may cross. Slow down, look and listen for trains, and be ready to stop if a train is nearby or signals activate. Never try to beat a train or go around lowered gates.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a highway divided by two solid yellow lines, when may you cross those lines?
options: a:To pass bicyclists at any time.,b:Whenever traffic ahead is moving slowly.,c:To pass slower traffic when safe.,d:Only to make a left turn into or from a private road
note: Two solid yellow lines in the center of the road mean no passing in either direction. You may only cross them to make a left turn into or from a driveway, alley, or private road, or when specifically directed by traffic control or emergency personnel.

question: At a railroad crossing with only a crossbuck and no gates or flashing lights, you should:
options: a:Drive quickly across to minimize time on the tracks.,b:Turn up the radio to listen for an approaching train.,c:Assume trains will always stop for vehicles.,d:Approach with extreme caution and cross only when you are sure no train is coming.
note: A crossbuck alone means you must treat the railroad crossing like a yield sign. Slow down, look and listen carefully in both directions, and cross only when you are sure no train is coming and there is enough space to clear the tracks completely.

question: What must a driver do when approaching a flashing red traffic signal?
options: a:Stop only if other vehicles are present.,b:Stop,c:Slow down and proceed without stopping.,d:Merge to the right and continue.
note: A flashing red light is treated the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, yield to any traffic and pedestrians with the right-of-way, and then proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe to go.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you approach an uncontrolled intersection?
options: a:Stop in the center of the road and wait for others to pass.,b:Slow down,c:Maintain your speed and proceed without checking.,d:Only yield if you see a stop sign.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, there are no stop or yield signs, so you must use extra caution. Slow down, scan left-right-left, be ready to brake, and yield to vehicles already in the intersection and to vehicles coming from your right if you arrive at the same time.

question: How can you ensure your physical condition won't make driving unsafe?
options: a:Rely on passengers to handle driving if you feel unwell.,b:Only drive when perfectly healthy with no medications ever.,c:Know how any medicines affect your driving,d:Ignore minor physical issues and drive anyway.
note: Knowing how any medicines affect your driving is essential. Many prescription and over‑the‑counter drugs can cause drowsiness, blurred vision, or slower reaction time. Always read labels, follow medical advice, and avoid driving if a medication or health condition could impair your ability to see, think clearly, or react quickly.

question: What is the only effective method to lower your BAC?
options: a:Drink coffee.,b:Exercise.,c:Allow your body time to remove the alcohol.
note: Only time allows your body to lower its blood alcohol concentration. The liver can process only a certain amount of alcohol per hour, and nothing—coffee, exercise, cold showers, or food—can speed this up. You must wait until your body has fully metabolized the alcohol before you are safe to drive.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a roadway from a private road or driveway you should:
options: a:Stop with part of your car in the roadway to warn others.,b:Blow your horn to alert traffic.,c:Drive quickly to merge with traffic.,d:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and vehicles already on the roadway.
note: When entering a roadway from a private road or driveway, you must yield to all pedestrians and vehicles already on the road. Stop if necessary, look carefully in all directions, and only enter when there is a safe gap. Never pull out to force other drivers to slow or swerve.

question: Which in-vehicle distraction most increases crash risk?
options: a:Adjusting the seat before driving.,b:Playing the radio at moderate volume.,c:Using a CD player to change tracks occasionally.,d:Using a cell phone
note: Using a cell phone while driving is one of the most dangerous in‑vehicle distractions because it takes your attention away from the road mentally and often visually and manually. Even hands‑free calls reduce your focus on driving, increasing the risk of missing hazards and being involved in a crash.

question: What helps a person overcome the effects of alcoholic drinks?
options: a:Only the passage of time.,b:Hot coffee and fresh air.,c:Tomato juice and lime.,d:Exercising vigorously.
note: Only the passage of time reduces the effects of alcohol. Your body must metabolize the alcohol through normal processes, and this cannot be sped up by coffee, fresh air, food, or exercise. Until enough time has passed, your judgment, coordination, and reaction time can remain impaired.

question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, you must:
options: a:Slow down and continue driving.,b:Speed up to get out of the way.,c:Drive with your flashers on.,d:Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
note: When an emergency vehicle using sirens and flashing lights approaches from behind, you must safely pull over to the right side of the road and stop until it has passed. This creates a clear path so the emergency vehicle can move quickly and safely. Do not speed up, continue driving, or use your flashers instead of yielding.

question: What is the proper method to check your blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Use your peripheral vision without turning your head.,b:Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.,c:Look into the side mirror only.,d:Look into the rearview mirror.
note: To check your blind spot before changing lanes, quickly look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move. Mirrors alone cannot show the entire area beside and slightly behind your vehicle, so a shoulder check is necessary to be sure no vehicle, motorcycle, bicycle, or pedestrian is in that hidden area.

question: Which factor does vehicle stopping distance NOT depend on?
options: a:The time of day.,b:Your reaction time.,c:The condition of your brakes.,d:The road surface and weather.
note: Stopping distance is the total distance your vehicle travels from the moment you see a hazard until you come to a complete stop. It depends on your reaction time, the condition of your brakes and tires, your speed, and road and weather conditions. The time of day by itself does not directly change how far it takes your vehicle to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before turning, you should:
options: a:Use your signal several seconds before making the turn.,b:Increase your speed to create a gap.,c:Turn the wheel abruptly without signaling.,d:Honk to warn other drivers before turning.
note: Before turning, you should signal well in advance—typically at least 100 feet or about three to four seconds before the turn—so other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians know your intentions. After signaling, slow down as needed and complete the turn safely and smoothly.

question: On average, how much alcohol does the human body eliminate per hour?
options: a:About three drinks per hour.,b:None,c:About one standard drink per hour.,d:About two drinks per hour.
note: The body typically processes alcohol at a rate of about one standard drink per hour, though this can vary with body size, sex, health, and other factors. Because the body can only eliminate alcohol slowly, drinking more than this rate quickly leads to impairment and higher blood alcohol concentration.

question: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, what is the best action?
options: a:Get out of the car and walk for help.,b:Stay in your car and wait for help.,c:Lay down in the car and sleep.,d:Stand on the road to signal other drivers.
note: If you are stranded in a snowstorm, you should stay with your vehicle. It provides shelter, makes you easier for rescuers to find, and protects you from getting lost or exposed to extreme cold. Run the engine only occasionally for heat, make sure the exhaust pipe is clear of snow to prevent carbon monoxide buildup, and wait for help.

question: If you begin feeling drowsy while driving, the safest choice is to:
options: a:Turn up the radio and keep going.,b:Drink coffee and continue driving.,c:Open a window to get fresh air.,d:Stop driving and rest.
note: Fatigue poses a serious risk similar to impairment from alcohol. If you feel tired while driving, stop and rest rather than trying short-term fixes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an officer is directing traffic at an intersection while lights are working, you should:
options: a:Follow the directions given by the officer rather than the traffic signals.,b:Follow the traffic light over the officer's instructions.,c:Honk to hurry the officer.,d:Ignore both and proceed with caution.
note: When a police officer or other authorized person is directing traffic, you must follow their hand signals and instructions, even if the traffic lights or signs say something different. Officers may override signals to manage crashes, road work, or congestion, and their directions control the intersection until they stop directing traffic.

question: Approaching a flashing red traffic light, drivers should:
options: a:Treat it like a stop sign and come to a complete stop.,b:Continue through if no other traffic is present.,c:Increase speed to clear the intersection quickly.,d:Wait for a police officer to direct traffic.
note: A flashing red traffic light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, then proceed only when traffic and pedestrians are clear and it is safe to go.

question: When driving at night and another vehicle approaches, which headlight setting should you use?
options: a:Parking lights only.,b:No lights.,c:High beams.,d:Low beams.
note: When driving at night and another vehicle is approaching, you must use low-beam headlights. High beams can blind or dazzle oncoming drivers, making it harder for them to see the road. Dim your high beams when you are within about 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle or when following another vehicle closely.

question: What should you do first if you must slow on a slippery surface?
options: a:Apply the brakes firmly.,b:Apply the parking brake.,c:Take your foot off the gas pedal.
note: On a slippery surface, your first action to slow down should be to gently take your foot off the accelerator. This lets the vehicle slow gradually using engine braking, which helps maintain traction. Braking hard right away can cause the wheels to lock or lose grip, leading to a skid. If you need to slow more after easing off the gas, apply the brakes gently and progressively.

question: Regulatory traffic signs are usually what color and how should drivers treat them?
options: a:White and they must always be obeyed.,b:Blue and they are optional.,c:Green and they are only suggestions.,d:Yellow and they warn of hazards.
note: Regulatory signs tell you about laws and rules you must follow, such as speed limits, lane use, and parking restrictions. In the U.S., these signs are usually white with black or red symbols or lettering. Because they state legal requirements, drivers are required to obey them at all times unless directed otherwise by a police officer or traffic control person.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it permissible to cross solid yellow center lines?
options: a:To pass another vehicle on a hill.,b:At any time to pass slower traffic.,c:Only during daylight hours.,d:Only to make a left turn into or from a private road.
note: A solid yellow center line means you may not cross it to pass other vehicles because it is unsafe to do so. However, you are allowed to cross solid yellow lines when you are making a left turn into or from a driveway, alley, or side road, as long as you yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. You should never use a solid yellow line area for passing on hills, curves, or anywhere your view is limited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is required to pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road?
options: a:You must use the lane belonging to oncoming traffic to complete the pass when it is safe and legal.,b:Never cross the centerline to pass.,c:Use the shoulder to pass when it is clear.,d:Flash your lights to tell the other vehicle to speed up.
note: On a two-lane, two-way road, passing usually requires you to move into the lane used by oncoming traffic. You may only do this where passing is allowed by the road markings and signs, and only when you have enough clear distance ahead to complete the pass safely without exceeding the speed limit. Never use the shoulder to pass, and never force another driver to speed up or slow suddenly for your pass.

question: On slick roads, you should:
options: a:Change lanes rapidly to avoid hazards.,b:Accelerate quickly to maintain control.,c:Take turns more slowly than usual and avoid abrupt maneuvers.,d:Drive the same as on dry roads.
note: On slick or slippery roads, your tires have less grip, so sudden steering, braking, or acceleration can easily cause a skid. You should slow down, take turns more slowly than usual, and make all movements—steering, braking, and accelerating—smooth and gradual. This helps your tires maintain traction and keeps the vehicle stable.

question: Any activity that requires you to do which of these could lead to a crash?
options: a:Take your eyes off the road,b:Take your attention away from driving.,c:Take your hands off the wheel
note: Any distraction that takes your eyes off the road, your mind off driving, or your hands off the wheel can lead to a crash. Visual, mental, and manual distractions all reduce your ability to react to hazards in time.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing with flashing signals, what is the correct action?
options: a:Stop no closer than 15 feet from the nearest rail while the signals warn of an approaching train.,b:Slow down and proceed if you do not see a train.,c:Speed through if you can clear the tracks quickly.,d:Cross and then look back for trains.
note: When the lights are flashing at a railroad crossing, you must stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail and remain stopped until the signals stop and it is clearly safe to cross. Never try to beat a train or drive around lowered gates.

question: What's the best way to avoid hydroplaning?
options: a:Inflate tires beyond recommended pressure to shed water.,b:Drive faster to pass over water quickly.,c:Slow down when roads are wet and avoid standing water,d:Use cruise control to stabilize speed.
note: To avoid hydroplaning, slow down when roads are wet, especially in heavy rain or where water pools on the surface. Avoid standing water and make sure your tires have good tread and are properly inflated so they can channel water away.

question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means:
options: a:Stop and wait for a green light.,b:Slow down and proceed with care.,c:Continue through at normal speed.,d:Yield only to pedestrians.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed with caution. Look for cross traffic, pedestrians, and other hazards, and be prepared to stop if necessary, but you are not required to stop if the way is clear.

question: What best ensures safety when you back your vehicle?
options: a:Honk continuously while reversing.,b:Rely solely on rearview mirrors and backup camera.,c:Back rapidly to finish quickly.,d:Walk behind and check for obstacles before getting into the driver's seat.
note: Before backing, walk behind your vehicle to check for children, pedestrians, or objects you cannot see from the driver’s seat. Then back slowly while looking over your shoulder and using mirrors and cameras as aids, not as your only check.

question: When executing a turn, what should you do with your speed?
options: a:Increase your speed to complete the turn sooner.,b:Reduce your speed to maintain control.,c:Maintain the same speed you had before turning.,d:Vary your speed randomly during the turn.
note: When preparing to turn, you should slow down before the turn so you can stay in your lane, keep good control of the vehicle, and react if something unexpected happens. Enter the turn at a safe speed and then gently accelerate as you complete it.

question: If you are involved in a serious crash, which actions are required?
options: a:Only move the vehicles and do not call the police.,b:Continue driving if damage appears minor.,c:Report the crash only if you feel at fault.,d:Stop at the scene, check for injuries, call emergency services if needed, and follow state reporting requirements.
note: Stop your vehicle, check for injuries, call emergency services when needed, and report crashes to law enforcement when there is injury, death, or significant property damage.

question: If you are in the right lane of a multi-lane highway and want to move left, what should you do?
options: a:Only check your side mirror and then move left.,b:Accelerate and move left quickly.,c:Check your mirrors, signal, and glance over your shoulder to be sure the blind spot and the lane are clear before moving left.,d:Signal and change lanes without checking mirrors.
note: Before moving left on a multi-lane highway, check your mirrors to see traffic behind and beside you, signal to show your intention, and quickly glance over your left shoulder to check your blind spot. Only change lanes when the lane is clear and you can move safely.

question: Which document must the driver present when stopped for a violation or equipment check?
options: a:Proof of vehicle registration.,b:Driver's license.,c:Proof of insurance.
note: When stopped, a driver must present their license; they should also have registration and proof of insurance available in the vehicle.

question: As a pedestrian, what is the safest practice?
options: a:Cross at any point because drivers must stop.,b:Do not step into a street or crosswalk if vehicles are approaching closely.,c:Always insist on your right-of-way no matter vehicle distance.,d:Walk against traffic on sidewalks for safety.
note: Pedestrians should never step into the street or a crosswalk if a vehicle is so close that it cannot safely stop, even if they have the right-of-way. Make eye contact with drivers, wait for a safe gap, and only begin crossing when you are sure approaching vehicles can stop in time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is passing prohibited?
options: a:Only when a no-passing sign is posted.,b:Only when daytime visibility is poor.,c:Only on highways with multiple lanes.,d:At an intersection
note: Passing is prohibited in several situations because your view or the space to complete the pass safely is limited. You must not pass at or near intersections, on hills or curves where you cannot see far enough ahead, at railroad crossings, when a school bus has flashing red lights, or anywhere signs or pavement markings indicate a no‑passing zone.

question: A work zone may be:
options: a:Marked only with black and white signs.,b:Stationary or moving and is marked with orange signs,c:Restricted to times of road construction only.,d:Ignored if you are in a hurry.
note: Work zones can be either stationary (such as a fixed construction area) or moving (such as line painting or mowing). They are typically marked with orange warning signs, cones, or barrels. When you see these, slow down, be prepared for workers or equipment on or near the roadway, and follow all posted instructions.

question: If your tire blows out while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly,b:Keep driving at the same speed.,c:Slam on your brakes.,d:Turn off your headlights immediately.
note: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel firmly to keep control of the vehicle, and do not slam on the brakes. Ease your foot off the accelerator, let the car slow down gradually, then brake gently and steer to a safe place off the road. Sudden hard braking can cause you to lose control, especially at higher speeds.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway you should first:
options: a:Sound your horn to warn others.,b:Reduce your speed by half.,c:Check your rearview and side mirrors and look over your shoulder for blind spots.,d:Turn on your headlights.
note: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway, first check your rearview and side mirrors, then quickly look over your shoulder to check your blind spot in the direction you want to move. Signal your intention, make sure the lane is clear, and then change lanes smoothly. Simply turning on headlights does not ensure it is safe to change lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of these is a location where parking is prohibited?
options: a:Within 20 feet of a fire hydrant.,b:Within 200 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection.,c:In a private driveway with permission.,d:Within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.
note: You must not park within a certain distance of key locations so emergency access and visibility are maintained. Parking is prohibited within 15 feet of a fire hydrant and within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection, unless local law specifies a different distance. Always check your state’s specific distances, but 15 feet from a hydrant is a common standard.

question: You may pass another vehicle when the line dividing lanes is a ____ line.
options: a:Solid yellow.,b:Solid white.,c:Broken white.,d:Double solid yellow.
note: You may pass another vehicle when there is a broken (dashed) line on your side of the road. Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed to change lanes or pass when it is safe. Solid yellow or double solid yellow lines generally mean no passing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it illegal to drive below the speed limit?
options: a:When in a construction zone only.,b:When you're tired.,c:When driving slowly disrupts the normal flow of traffic.,d:Only in rural areas.
note: Driving significantly below the speed of surrounding traffic can be illegal if it unnecessarily blocks or impedes the normal flow of traffic. Even if you are at or below the posted limit, you must adjust your speed so you do not create a hazard or obstruction for other drivers.

question: Which statement about sudden weather changes is correct?
options: a:You should slow down in rain and fog.,b:You can drive the same as in clear weather.,c:You should increase your speed in rain to pass quickly.,d:You should ignore vehicles behind you in bad weather.
note: In sudden weather changes such as rain or fog, you should reduce your speed, increase following distance, and drive more cautiously. Slowing down gives you more time to react to reduced visibility and slippery roads, and helps you maintain control of the vehicle.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
options: a:Stop and wait for a green light.,b:You have the right-of-way.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.,d:Stop and look for other vehicles
note: A flashing yellow traffic light means you must slow down and proceed with caution. You do not have to stop, but you should be prepared to yield and carefully check for other vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians before entering the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which traffic signal requires you to come to a complete stop?
options: a:A steady yellow light.,b:A yellow arrow.,c:A steady green light.,d:A flashing red light.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign: you must come to a complete stop at the limit line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, then proceed only when it is safe and after yielding to any traffic or pedestrians with the right-of-way.

question: What can happen to a bicyclist who fails to obey traffic laws?
options: a:They will always receive just a warning from law enforcement.,b:They cannot be stopped by police.,c:They are always correct because they are more vulnerable.,d:They can be ticketed.
note: Bicyclists are generally required to follow the same traffic laws as motor vehicle drivers, such as stopping at red lights and stop signs and yielding when required. If they violate these laws, they can be stopped by police and issued citations just like drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway from an on-ramp, the best practice is to:
options: a:Accelerate on the ramp to match the speed of freeway traffic and merge safely.,b:Proceed slowly and wait for an opening at a much lower speed.,c:Turn on hazard lights until fully merged.,d:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a gap.
note: When entering a freeway, you should use the on‑ramp and acceleration lane to reach a speed close to that of traffic already on the freeway, then merge when it is safe. Stopping or entering at a much lower speed is dangerous because it disrupts traffic flow and increases the risk of a collision.

question: On roads with no sidewalks, which side should a pedestrian walk on?
options: a:The same side as traffic movement.,b:The side facing oncoming traffic (so they can see approaching vehicles).,c:The middle of the road for visibility.,d:The side with the heaviest traffic.
note: If there is no sidewalk, pedestrians should walk on the side of the road facing oncoming traffic. This allows them to see approaching vehicles and react if a driver drifts toward the shoulder, improving their safety.

question: How should you respond when approaching a flashing yellow traffic signal?
options: a:Come to a complete stop and wait until the light turns green.,b:Increase your speed to clear the area quickly.,c:Slow down, yield as needed, and proceed with caution.,d:Ignore the signal if the road looks clear.
note: A flashing yellow signal means you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution, yielding as necessary to other traffic and pedestrians. You are not required to stop unless conditions or other road users make it necessary for safety.

question: If you are in an accident and someone is injured, what should you do?
options: a:Do not move the injured unnecessarily, keep them warm and administer first aid as appropriate until help arrives.,b:Always move injured people to the nearest sidewalk immediately.,c:Leave the injured and seek help elsewhere.,d:Forcefully reposition injured limbs to reduce pain.
note: If someone is injured in a crash, call emergency services, do not move them unless there is an immediate danger (such as fire), keep them warm, and provide first aid only if you are trained. Moving an injured person unnecessarily can worsen neck, back, or other serious injuries.

question: Which measure may help drivers conserve gasoline?
options: a:Driving with lower tire pressure than recommended.,b:Slowing down and decelerating gradually rather than frequent hard braking.,c:Accelerating quickly whenever possible.,d:Idling the engine while parked to warm the car.
note: Anticipating traffic, keeping a steady speed, and slowing down gradually instead of braking hard helps you avoid wasting fuel on repeated heavy acceleration. Smooth driving reduces sudden speed changes, which improves fuel economy and reduces wear on your vehicle.

question: What effect can result from combining alcohol with drugs?
options: a:Decrease combined effects.,b:Increase the effects of both.,c:Help cure your illness.
note: Mixing alcohol with many prescription, over‑the‑counter, or illegal drugs usually increases the effects of both substances. This can greatly reduce coordination, judgment, and reaction time, making driving far more dangerous than using either one alone.

question: What is the most common color of warning signs?
options: a:Blue.,b:Red.,c:Green.,d:Yellow.
note: Most general warning signs are yellow diamonds with black symbols or words. They alert you to conditions such as curves, intersections, or pedestrian crossings so you can slow down and proceed with caution.

question: What hazard can a leaking exhaust system create for vehicle occupants?
options: a:It forces you to have tune-ups more often.,b:It causes excessive oil consumption.,c:It can make you drowsy or cause death from toxic fumes.
note: A leaking exhaust system can let carbon monoxide and other poisonous gases enter the passenger compartment. Breathing these fumes can make you drowsy, impair your driving, and in high enough concentrations can cause unconsciousness or death.

question: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is affected by all of the following EXCEPT:
options: a:The type of alcoholic beverage you drink.,b:Your body weight.,c:How much alcohol you consume.,d:How much time passes between drinks.
note: Your BAC depends mainly on how much alcohol you drink, how quickly you drink it, and your body weight. A standard amount of beer, wine, or liquor contains about the same amount of pure alcohol, so the “type” of drink matters less than the total alcohol you consume and the time over which you consume it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic signals are out at an intersection due to a power outage, you should:
options: a:Park and wait for power to be restored.,b:Turn on your hazard lights and proceed without stopping.,c:Treat the intersection like a four-way stop and yield to others appropriately.,d:Use hand signals to direct other vehicles.
note: When a traffic signal is completely out, the intersection must be treated as a four‑way stop. Come to a complete stop, then proceed in turn, yielding to vehicles that arrived first or are already in the intersection, and to pedestrians.

question: An advisory speed sign for a curve should be treated how in bad weather?
options: a:Reduce speed below the advisory limit when roads are wet, snowy, or icy.,b:Be ignored if you are comfortable driving faster.,c:Follow only when traffic is heavy.,d:Increase speed to maintain momentum.
note: Advisory speed signs show a safe speed for ideal, dry conditions. In rain, snow, ice, or poor visibility, you should slow down even more below the advisory speed to maintain traction and control.

question: When preparing to change lanes you should not:
options: a:Check side and rearview mirrors.,b:Signal to indicate your intentions.,c:Ensure the lane is clear before entering.,d:Fail to check for other drivers who might be moving into the same lane.
note: Before changing lanes, always check mirrors, signal, and look for other vehicles that may be moving into the same lane. Failing to check for others entering the lane is unsafe and can lead to side‑swipe collisions.

question: Lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions are divided by what color lines?
options: a:White lines.,b:Blue lines.,c:Yellow lines.,d:Red lines.
note: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction, while other colors are used for special purposes such as parking or restricted areas.

question: In traffic, what is the safest speed choice relative to other vehicles?
options: a:Vary speed frequently to stay alert.,b:Drive faster than the flow of traffic to stay ahead.,c:Drive with the flow of traffic within the posted limits.,d:Drive much slower than traffic to be cautious.
note: The safest choice is to travel with the general flow of traffic while staying within the posted speed limit. Driving much faster or much slower than surrounding traffic increases the risk of crashes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may proceed carefully through an intersection with a yellow light if:
options: a:You are already within the intersection when the light turns yellow.,b:You are speeding to clear the intersection quickly.,c:There are pedestrians crossing.,d:You intend to make a U-turn.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, you should continue through carefully rather than stop suddenly. If you have not yet entered the intersection, you should slow down and stop if you can do so safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To enter a freeway safely from an on-ramp you should:
options: a:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for cars to pull over.,b:Enter slowly and expect freeway traffic to yield.,c:Enter at any speed because entering traffic has the right-of-way.,d:Signal, use the acceleration lane to match freeway speed, and yield to traffic already on the freeway.
note: When entering a freeway, use the on‑ramp and acceleration lane to build up speed so you can match the flow of traffic. Signal, check mirrors and blind spots, and yield to vehicles already on the freeway. Do not stop at the end of the ramp unless absolutely necessary, and do not expect freeway traffic to move over for you.

question: How does increasing your vehicle speed affect your field of vision?
options: a:Speed has no effect on vision.,b:It increases your field of vision and awareness.,c:It makes it easier to see cross traffic.,d:It decreases your field of vision
note: As your speed increases, your field of vision narrows. You see less to the sides and must look farther ahead to spot hazards in time. This is why high speeds require extra caution and attention to scanning the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an intersection where you wish to turn but are not in the correct lane, what should you do?
options: a:Turn from your current lane without signaling.,b:Proceed to the next intersection and make the turn from the proper lane.,c:Back up to position yourself for the turn.,d:Quickly cut across traffic to make the turn.
note: If you are not in the correct lane to make a turn when you reach an intersection, continue straight and go to the next intersection. Then get into the proper lane and make your turn safely. Never make sudden lane changes, turn from the wrong lane, or back up in an intersection.

question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?
options: a:When directed by a flagger.,b:All of the above.,c:When controlled by a stop sign.,d:When flashing red signals and gates are operating.
note: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger directs you to stop, when there is a stop sign requiring a stop, and when flashing red lights or gates indicate a train is approaching. Always obey these controls and never go around lowered gates or ignore warning signals.

question: Which factors affect braking distance?
options: a:The pavement condition.,b:All of the above.,c:The vehicle's speed.,d:The condition of brakes and tires.
note: Braking distance is affected by several factors working together. The faster you are going, the longer it takes to stop. Worn or poorly maintained brakes and tires increase stopping distance, and slippery or uneven pavement also makes it harder to stop quickly. Because speed, brake and tire condition, and road surface all matter, all of the listed factors affect braking distance.

question: What is a 'No zone' in relation to large vehicles?
options: a:A designated no passing zone on highways.,b:A school bus loading area.,c:A one-way traffic area on city streets.,d:The large blind spot areas around trucks where the truck driver cannot see you.
note: A 'No Zone' is the large blind spot area around trucks and other large vehicles where the driver cannot see you in their mirrors. These areas are along the sides, directly behind, and sometimes directly in front of the truck. You should avoid driving in these blind spots for long periods, because the truck driver may not know you are there and could change lanes or stop suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, which vehicle has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle on the left has the right-of-way.,b:Both should proceed simultaneously without yielding.,c:Yield to the largest vehicle first.,d:The vehicle on the right has the right-of-way
note: At a four-way stop, when two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This rule helps decide who goes first when arrival is simultaneous. If vehicles arrive at different times, the one that stops first goes first, after checking that it is safe.

question: How does alcohol affect your abilities as it accumulates in your blood?
options: a:Speeds up your reactions.,b:Improves coordination.,c:Slows down your reactions.,d:Makes you feel less confident.
note: As alcohol builds up in your bloodstream, it slows your brain and nervous system. Your reaction time becomes slower, your coordination and judgment get worse, and you are more likely to make driving errors. Alcohol often makes people feel more confident, but that confidence is false; your actual driving ability is reduced even if you feel more relaxed or bold.

question: Many crashes are caused by drivers who:
options: a:Travel too fast for the current road conditions.,b:Consistently check mirrors and blind spots.,c:Yield the right-of-way appropriately.,d:Follow all traffic laws.
note: Many crashes happen because drivers travel too fast for current conditions, even if they are at or below the posted speed limit. Rain, snow, fog, heavy traffic, curves, and poor visibility all require you to slow down. Safe drivers adjust their speed to match road, traffic, and weather conditions so they have enough time and distance to react.

question: How can you avoid needing to make emergency stops in traffic?
options: a:Drive only in the right lane.,b:Honk frequently to alert others.,c:Look ahead and maintain a safe following distance.,d:Follow the car in front of you closely.
note: Looking well ahead and keeping a safe following distance gives you time to see problems early and slow down smoothly instead of slamming on the brakes. Tailgating or relying on your horn does not prevent emergencies and increases your crash risk.

question: When should you increase your following distance?
options: a:When following a large vehicle that blocks your view.,b:Only when exiting an expressway.,c:Only when behind a motorcycle.,d:Never, keep the same distance at all times.
note: You should increase following distance whenever you need more time to see and react, such as when a large vehicle blocks your view, in bad weather, at higher speeds, or when you feel pressured or tired. More space gives you a better view and more time to stop safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You want to turn left at a green light but heavy oncoming traffic exists. What should you do?
options: a:Wait behind the stop line until oncoming traffic clears completely.,b:Make a U-turn instead.,c:Enter the intersection on green, yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, and wait for a safe gap to complete your left turn.,d:Proceed into the crosswalk to wait for a gap.
note: For a left turn on a green light without a green arrow, you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. When the intersection is clear, move into it and wait with your wheels straight until there is a safe gap. If the light turns yellow or red while you are already in the intersection, you should complete the turn when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If turning onto a street with multiple lanes traveling in your direction, which lane should you enter?
options: a:The far left lane always.,b:The lane nearest to the lane you came from (the closest lane moving in your direction).,c:The middle lane only.,d:Any lane as long as you signal.
note: When turning onto a multi-lane road, you must turn into the lane closest to you that is going in your direction. This keeps traffic organized and prevents conflicts with vehicles turning from other directions or changing lanes at the same time.

question: What should you do if your accelerator sticks while driving?
options: a:Reach down and attempt to pull it up.,b:Shift to neutral and apply steady pressure on the brake.,c:Shift to park immediately.,d:Turn the steering wheel sharply to stop.
note: If the accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road, shift to neutral, and apply steady pressure on the brakes. Steer to the side of the road and stop in a safe place, then turn off the engine. Do not turn the engine off while moving at speed or shift to park, as this can cause loss of control.

question: While backing, what is the recommended technique?
options: a:Open the driver's door and lean out to see.,b:Turn your head and look through the rear window,c:Rely exclusively on mirrors and sensors.,d:Back quickly to minimize time spent reversing.
note: When backing, you should turn your head and look directly through the rear window so you can clearly see the path behind you. Mirrors and sensors are only aids and must not replace a direct visual check. Back slowly and be prepared to stop if anything enters your path.

question: What do pennant-shaped signs (sideways triangular) typically indicate?
options: a:Yield ahead.,b:School zones.,c:Speed limits.,d:No passing zones.
note: Pennant-shaped signs, which are sideways triangles pointing to the right, are used to mark no passing zones. They warn you that it is unsafe and illegal to pass in that area, usually due to limited visibility or other hazards.

question: Approximately how far might a loaded tractor-trailer travel before stopping from 55 mph?
options: a:125 feet,b:400 feet.,c:50 feet
note: A fully loaded tractor-trailer needs a much longer distance to stop than a passenger car. At about 55 mph, a large truck may need close to 400 feet to come to a complete stop under good conditions. This longer stopping distance is why you should never cut closely in front of a truck and should allow extra space when merging or changing lanes near them.

question: Car drivers should remember that large trucks:
options: a:Are as maneuverable as small cars in tight spaces.,b:Can stop more quickly than passenger cars.,c:Do not require extra following distance.,d:Have large blind spots and require extra room to maneuver and stop.
note: Large trucks have sizable blind spots on all sides and need more space to turn, change lanes, and stop. Because of their weight, they generally take longer to stop than passenger cars. Give trucks extra room, avoid driving in their blind spots, and do not cut in front of them.

question: When parking uphill next to a curb, you should:
options: a:Leave the car in neutral to prevent rolling.,b:Set the parking brake and keep rear tires against the curb.,c:Set the parking brake and keep front tires straight.,d:Set the parking brake and turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your front wheels away from the curb and set the parking brake. If the vehicle rolls, the back of the front tire will move toward the curb and the curb will help stop the vehicle from rolling into traffic.

question: How should you respond to a flashing red traffic signal at an intersection?
options: a:Treat it like a circular green light.,b:Come to a full stop,c:Slow down and go without stopping.,d:Stop only if other vehicles are approaching.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for cross traffic and pedestrians, yield as needed, and then proceed only when it is safe.

question: When driving on slippery roads, you should:
options: a:Use cruise control to maintain a steady speed.,b:Change lanes frequently to find better traction.,c:Increase your following distance to allow more stopping time.,d:Drive at the posted speed limit regardless of conditions.
note: On slippery roads your stopping distance increases because traction is reduced. You should slow down and increase your following distance so you have more time and space to stop smoothly and avoid skids.

question: What actions should you take when approaching railroad tracks?
options: a:Look and listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.,b:Speed up to cross before gates lower.,c:Drive around a lowered gate if you can.,d:Stop on the tracks to look both ways.
note: When approaching railroad tracks, slow down, look and listen carefully for trains, and be prepared to stop if a train is approaching. Never try to beat a train, and never drive around or under lowered gates.

question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?
options: a:Check mirrors and blind spots before stopping.,b:Avoid sudden stops.,c:Release the gas to let the car slow before braking.,d:All of the above.
note: To help prevent rear-end collisions, avoid sudden stops by easing off the accelerator early and braking smoothly, and always check your mirrors and blind spots before slowing or stopping so drivers behind you have time to react.

question: If you see the driver ahead driving with one hand and talking to a passenger, you should:
options: a:Honk to get their attention.,b:Give that vehicle extra space because the driver may be inattentive.,c:Try to outdrive them.,d:Follow closely to monitor their behavior.
note: A driver who is distracted or not fully in control may react slowly or unpredictably. Give that vehicle extra space so you have more time to respond if they drift, brake suddenly, or make an unexpected maneuver.

question: Orange-colored traffic signs typically indicate:
options: a:School zones.,b:Work zones or construction areas.,c:Service facilities.,d:Regulatory instructions.
note: Orange traffic signs are used for temporary traffic control in work zones. They warn of construction, maintenance, or utility operations and alert you to slow down, be prepared for workers, equipment, lane shifts, or other changes in normal traffic patterns.

question: Two solid white lines across a lane indicate a crosswalk; as a driver, you should:
options: a:No one has right-of-way.,b:Always yield to pedestrians in crosswalks.,c:Motor vehicles have right-of-way.,d:Only yield when lights flash.
note: Two solid white lines across the lane mark a crosswalk. Drivers must always yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in marked or unmarked crosswalks. Be prepared to slow or stop when pedestrians are in or about to enter the crosswalk, and do not proceed until they are safely out of your path.

question: If another vehicle is following you too closely, you should:
options: a:Gradually slow and, when safe, change lanes or allow them to pass; avoid sudden braking.,b:Brake-check them to force them back.,c:Turn on high beams repeatedly to annoy them.,d:Speed up to put distance between you.
note: If someone is following too closely, increase your following distance ahead and gradually slow so they can pass when it is safe. Avoid sudden or aggressive braking, which can cause a rear-end collision. If needed, change lanes or pull over safely to let the tailgater go by.

question: Which statement about driving on wet roadways is true?
options: a:Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.,b:Wet roads improve braking.,c:Your tires become less effective at clearing water as speed increases.,d:Water does not affect cars with good tires.
note: On wet roads, as your speed increases, your tires have less time to squeeze water out from under the tread. This makes it easier to lose contact with the road and hydroplane. To reduce this risk, slow down in rain, especially in standing water or during the first minutes of a storm.

question: What do downward-pointing triangular traffic signs typically indicate?
options: a:Speed limits.,b:Yield to other traffic or pedestrians.,c:Construction work ahead.,d:School zones.
note: A downward-pointing triangle is the standard shape for a yield sign. It tells you to slow down, be ready to stop, and give the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians already in or close to the intersection or roadway you are entering.

question: If you're on a one-way street and an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches, what must you do?
options: a:Speed up and take the nearest exit.,b:Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop.,c:Pull to the left and stop.,d:Turn on your hazard lights and continue.
note: On a one‑way street, you still must yield to emergency vehicles using lights or sirens. Move safely and promptly toward the nearest edge of the roadway (right or left), parallel to the curb, and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed, unless otherwise directed by officials.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you verify before passing on a multilane highway?
